records.literal_gloss: And it came about in the being him in a certain place praying, when he ceased, said one of the disciples of him to him, Lord, teach us to pray, just as also John taught the disciples of him.

en.L: And it happened, while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was praying in a certain place, [that] when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stopped, one of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, teach us to pray, just as John also taught his disciples."
en.B: Once Jesus was praying in a certain place. When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had finished, one of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, teach us how to pray, the way John taught his own disciples."
en.R: One time Jesus was praying in a certain place. When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} finished, one of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, please teach us how to pray. John taught his disciples how to pray."

es.R: Una vez Jesús estaba orando en un lugar. Cuando terminó, uno de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «Señor, por favor, enséñanos a orar. Juan les enseñó a orar a sus discípulos».

decisions.choice: praying: Luke shows Jesus at prayer before he teaches about prayer
decisions.reason: Luke often shows Jesus praying at turning points (3:21; 5:16; 6:12; 9:18, 28-29). Here the disciples see him pray and ask him to teach them.

decisions.choice: as John taught his disciples: a teacher gave his followers a way of praying of their own
decisions.reason: John's disciples were known for their prayers (5:33). A prayer given by a teacher marked out his followers as a group. The disciple asks Jesus for a prayer for those who follow him.

decisions.choice: Lord: a title of respect for Jesus as teacher and master
decisions.reason: The word can be a polite "sir", but a disciple uses it here of the one he follows, and Luke's readers hear in it the title of the risen Jesus (2:11).

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus at the start of a new section.

decisions.choice: two sentences: the request, then John's example
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the request short and gives the comparison as its own sentence.

source.text: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτοῖς· Ὅταν προσεύχησθε, λέγετε· Πάτερ, ἁγιασθήτω τὸ ὄνομά σου· ἐλθέτω ἡ βασιλεία σου·

records.literal_gloss: He said then to them, When you pray, say, Father, let be hallowed the name of you; let come the kingdom of you;

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "When you pray, say: 'Father, let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name be held holy; let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} kingdom come.
en.B: He said to them, "When you pray, say: 'Father, may {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name be honored as holy. May {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} kingdom come.
en.R: Jesus said to them, "When you pray, say this: 'Father, may {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name be treated as holy. May {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} kingdom come.

es.L: Y les dijo: «Cuando {{plural_you:oren|oréis}}, {{plural_you:digan|decid}}: “Padre, sea santificado {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nombre; venga {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} reino.

es.R: Jesús les dijo: «Cuando {{plural_you:oren|oréis}}, {{plural_you:digan|decid}} esto: “Padre, que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nombre sea tratado como santo. Que venga {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} reino.

sw.R: Yesu akawaambia, "Mnapoomba, semeni hivi: 'Baba, jina {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}} na litendewe kama jina takatifu. Ufalme {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} na uje.

decisions.choice: Father ... let your kingdom come: Luke's shorter form, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: "Our Father who is in heaven" and "let your will be done, as in heaven, so also on earth", the reading of many later manuscripts
a prayer for the Holy Spirit to come and cleanse us, in place of the prayer for the kingdom, found in a very few manuscripts and early writers
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts fill out Luke's prayer with words from the longer form in Matthew 6:9-10: "our ... who is in heaven" after "Father", and a request that God's will be done on earth as in heaven. The oldest manuscripts, including the papyrus P75 and Codex Vaticanus, have the shorter form. Scribes were far more likely to make Luke match the better-known form in Matthew than to shorten it. A very few witnesses have a request for the Holy Spirit instead of the request for the kingdom. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Father: God addressed directly as Father
decisions.reason: Jesus himself prays to God as "Father" (10:21; 22:42; 23:34, 46), and he gives his disciples the same way of speaking to God. Luke has the one word, without the additions found in Matthew.

decisions.choice: let your name be held holy: may God be honored as the holy God he is
decisions.reason: God's name stands for God himself as he has made himself known. The request is that his name be treated as holy by all people, and that God himself show his holiness, as he promised to do (Ezekiel 36:22-23). The passive form leaves both in view.

decisions.choice: let your kingdom come: may God's rule come in full
decisions.reason: Jesus proclaims the kingdom of God (4:43; 8:1) and sends his disciples to say it has come near (10:9, 11). The prayer asks God to bring his rule in its fullness.

decisions.choice: let ... be held holy (L); may ... be honored as holy (B); may ... be treated as holy (R)
decisions.reason: "Hallowed" is the familiar word in this prayer, but it is no longer used in everyday speech. Each level says what it means.

decisions.choice: the prayer is a quotation inside Jesus' words, in single quotation marks; it closes at the end of 11:4
decisions.reason: Jesus gives the words of the prayer inside his own speech.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus where the Greek has a pronoun or leaves the subject unstated, so young readers can follow who is acting.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:oren|oréis}}, {{plural_you:digan|decid}}
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to the disciples as a group, so every plural "you" and its verb is the reader setting: "ustedes" (Latin America, the default) or "vosotros" (Spain). English has no such choice. The same through this chapter.

decisions.choice: «Padre», with nothing added
alternatives: Padre nuestro que estás en los cielos
decisions.reason: Luke's prayer opens with the single word "Father" (meaning decisions m1, m2). Spanish readers know Matthew's longer opening, "Padre nuestro que estás en los cielos", by heart; it is not added here, so that Luke's shorter form stands as it is written.

decisions.choice: 'Baba', with nothing added
decisions.reason: Luke's prayer opens with the single word "Father" (meaning decisions m1, m2). Swahili readers know Matthew's longer opening, "Baba yetu uliye mbinguni", by heart; it is not added here, so that Luke's shorter form stands as it is written.

source.text: τὸν ἄρτον ἡμῶν τὸν ἐπιούσιον δίδου ἡμῖν τὸ καθ’ ἡμέραν·

records.literal_gloss: The bread of us the daily give to us each day;

en.L: Our daily bread give us each day;
en.B: Each day give us the bread we need.
en.R: Give us the food we need for each day.

es.L: Nuestro pan cotidiano danos cada día;
es.B: Danos cada día el pan que necesitamos.
es.R: Danos la comida que necesitamos para cada día.

sw.L: Mkate wetu wa kila siku utupe siku kwa siku;
sw.B: Kila siku utupe mkate tunaouhitaji.
sw.R: Utupe chakula tunachohitaji kwa kila siku.

decisions.choice: daily: the bread needed for the day
alternatives: for tomorrow, for the coming day
for the age to come, the bread of the kingdom
decisions.reason: The adjective (epiousios) is found almost nowhere outside this prayer (here and Matthew 6:11). In the third century Origen already said he knew it from no other Greek writing. It may be built from words meaning "the coming [day]" or from words meaning "being, existence". "Daily" goes back to the oldest Latin versions and fits the request "each day". Either way the prayer asks God for the food his people need, one day at a time.

decisions.choice: bread given each day: as God gave the manna day by day
alternatives: a store of food for the future
decisions.reason: In the wilderness God gave the manna each day, enough for that day (Exodus 16:4). Luke's "each day" and the present tense of "give" make it a request repeated day after day; Matthew 6:11 has "today".

decisions.choice: bread: food in general
decisions.reason: Bread was the main food of every meal, and the word often stands for food as a whole.

decisions.choice: Our daily bread first
alternatives: Give us each day our daily bread
decisions.reason: The Greek puts the bread first, for emphasis. Literal keeps that order.

decisions.choice: the bread we need (B); the food we need for each day (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly what is asked for: what we need for the day. "Daily bread" is kept at Literal.

source.text: καὶ ἄφες ἡμῖν τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν, καὶ γὰρ αὐτοὶ ἀφίομεν παντὶ ὀφείλοντι ἡμῖν· καὶ μὴ εἰσενέγκῃς ἡμᾶς εἰς πειρασμόν.

records.literal_gloss: and forgive us the sins of us, also for ourselves we forgive everyone being indebted to us; and not lead us into temptation.

en.L: and forgive us our sins, for we ourselves also forgive everyone owing us; and do not lead us into temptation.'"
en.B: Forgive us our sins, since we also forgive all who owe us. And do not bring us into temptation.'"
en.R: Forgive us for our sins, because we forgive everyone who has done wrong to us. And keep us away from temptation.'"

es.L: y perdónanos nuestros pecados, pues también nosotros mismos perdonamos a todo el que nos debe; y no nos introduzcas en tentación”».
es.B: Perdónanos nuestros pecados, ya que también nosotros perdonamos a todos los que nos deben. Y no nos hagas entrar en la tentación”».
es.R: Perdónanos nuestros pecados, porque nosotros perdonamos a todos los que nos han hecho mal. Y aléjanos de la tentación”».

sw.L: na utusamehe dhambi zetu, kwa maana sisi wenyewe pia tunamsamehe kila mtu anayetudai; na usituingize katika jaribu.'"
sw.B: Utusamehe dhambi zetu, kwa kuwa sisi pia tunawasamehe wote wanaotudai. Wala usitulete katika majaribu.'"
sw.R: Utusamehe dhambi zetu, kwa sababu tunawasamehe wote waliotukosea. Na utuepushe na majaribu.'"

decisions.choice: everyone owing us: everyone who has wronged us
alternatives: only those who owe us money
decisions.reason: A wrong done to someone is pictured as a debt owed to them, as in the story of the two debtors (7:41-47). Matthew 6:12 speaks of debts in both halves of the request; Luke has "sins" for what we owe God and keeps the picture of debt for what others owe us.

decisions.choice: for we ourselves also forgive: those who ask God's forgiveness forgive others
decisions.reason: The present tense describes a settled practice. Those who ask God to forgive them do not hold others' wrongs against them (6:37; 17:3-4). The prayer does not make our forgiving the price of God's; it shows what kind of people pray it.

decisions.choice: temptation: a testing that could lead to sin or falling away
decisions.reason: The word covers both being tempted to do wrong (4:13) and being tested by hardship or opposition (8:13; 22:28). Jesus tells the disciples to pray that they may not enter into it (22:40, 46). The request asks God to keep his people from such testing and from falling in it; God himself tempts no one to sin (James 1:13).

decisions.choice: the prayer ends with "into temptation", as in the SBLGNT
alternatives: "but deliver us from evil" added, as in many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add the request "but rescue us from evil" from Matthew 6:13. The oldest manuscripts, including P75 and Codex Vaticanus, end the prayer here. The closing words of praise known from later use of Matthew's prayer are not found in any manuscript of Luke. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: all who owe us (B); everyone who has done wrong to us (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of debt; Readable says what the debt stands for.

decisions.choice: keep us away from temptation
alternatives: do not lead us into temptation
decisions.reason: Readable puts the request in positive words: the one praying asks God not to bring them into temptation, that is, to keep them from it.

decisions.choice: jaribu (L); majaribu (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word is a testing that could lead to sin or falling away (meaning decision m3). "Jaribu" covers both a trial and a temptation, as the Greek does; "kishawishi" would be only an enticement to sin.

source.text: Καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Τίς ἐξ ὑμῶν ἕξει φίλον καὶ πορεύσεται πρὸς αὐτὸν μεσονυκτίου καὶ εἴπῃ αὐτῷ· Φίλε, χρῆσόν μοι τρεῖς ἄρτους, ἐπειδὴ φίλος μου παρεγένετο ἐξ ὁδοῦ πρός με καὶ οὐκ ἔχω ὃ παραθήσω αὐτῷ·

records.literal_gloss: And he said to them, Who of you will have a friend and will go to him at midnight and say to him, Friend, lend me three loaves, \v 6 since a friend of me has come from a journey to me and nothing I have what I will set before him;

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Which of you will have a friend, and will go to him at midnight and say to him, 'Friend, lend me three loaves, \v 6 since a friend of mine has come to me from a journey, and I have nothing to set before him,'
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Imagine that one of you has a friend, and you go to his house in the middle of the night and say to him, 'My friend, lend me three loaves. \v 6 Another friend of mine has come to my house from a journey, and I have nothing to set out for him to eat.'
en.R: Then Jesus said to them, "Suppose one of you goes to a friend's house in the middle of the night. You say to him, 'Friend, please lend me three loaves of bread. \v 6 A friend of mine has been traveling, and he has just come to stay with me. I do not have any food to give him.'

es.L: Y les dijo: «¿Quién de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} tendrá un amigo, e irá a él a medianoche y le dirá: “Amigo, préstame tres panes, \v 6 pues un amigo mío ha llegado a mí de viaje, y no tengo qué ofrecerle”,
es.B: Luego les dijo: «{{plural_you:Imaginen|Imaginad}} que uno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} tiene un amigo, y a medianoche va a su casa y le dice: “Amigo mío, préstame tres panes. \v 6 Otro amigo mío ha llegado de viaje a mi casa, y no tengo nada que servirle de comer”.
es.R: Luego Jesús les dijo: «{{plural_you:Supongan|Suponed}} que uno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} va a la casa de un amigo en medio de la noche. Le dice: “Amigo, por favor, préstame tres panes. \v 6 Un amigo mío ha estado de viaje y acaba de llegar a quedarse conmigo. No tengo comida para darle”.

sw.L: Kisha akawaambia, "Ni nani kwenu atakayekuwa na rafiki, naye atamwendea usiku wa manane na kumwambia, 'Rafiki, nikopeshe mikate mitatu, \v 6 kwa kuwa rafiki yangu amenijia kutoka safarini, nami sina kitu cha kumwandalia,'
sw.B: Kisha akawaambia, "Fikirieni kwamba mmoja wenu ana rafiki, naye anakwenda nyumbani kwake usiku wa manane na kumwambia, 'Rafiki yangu, nikopeshe mikate mitatu. \v 6 Rafiki yangu mwingine amefika nyumbani kwangu kutoka safarini, nami sina chakula cha kumpa ale.'
sw.R: Kisha Yesu akawaambia, "Tuseme mmoja wenu anakwenda nyumbani kwa rafiki yake usiku wa manane. Anamwambia, 'Rafiki, tafadhali nikopeshe mikate mitatu. \v 6 Rafiki yangu mmoja amekuwa safarini, na sasa amefika kukaa kwangu. Sina chakula chochote cha kumpa.'

decisions.choice: which of you will have a friend ...: a question that runs on to 11:7 and expects the answer "none of you"
alternatives: a plain statement about one person
decisions.reason: The question begins here and runs through the sleeper's answer in 11:7. Jesus asks his hearers whether they can imagine a friend turning them away: no one would expect that. 11:8 then adds that even if friendship were not enough, the man would still get up.

decisions.choice: a guest at midnight: welcoming a traveler with food was a duty
alternatives: an ordinary request at a convenient time
decisions.reason: Travelers often went on through the evening. To welcome a guest and set food before him was a duty that Scripture honors (Genesis 18:1-8). Bread was usually baked each day, so by night a household might have none left.

decisions.choice: three loaves: small flat loaves, enough for a meal
decisions.reason: Loaves were small and round. Three would make a meal for a guest, with some to spare.

decisions.choice: Imagine that one of you (B); Suppose one of you (R)
alternatives: Which of you will have a friend ...?
decisions.reason: The Greek question is long and runs into 11:7. Balanced and Readable start it as a story the hearers are asked to picture.

decisions.choice: to my house (B); to stay with me (R); for him to eat (B)
decisions.reason: The friend has come to the man's home as a guest. Balanced and Readable say so.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus where the Greek has a pronoun or leaves the subject unstated, so young readers can follow who is acting.

decisions.choice: uno de ustedes ... va ... le dice (the man in the third person)
decisions.reason: The English Balanced and Readable go on with "you go ... you say". Spanish, after "uno de ustedes", keeps the man who knocks in the third person, since switching from "ustedes" to "tú" in the middle of the sentence reads awkwardly; the same in 11:7-8. The meaning is unchanged.

decisions.choice: mmoja wenu ... anakwenda ... anamwambia (the man in the third person)
decisions.reason: The English Balanced and Readable go on with "you go ... you say". Swahili, after "mmoja wenu", keeps the man who knocks in the third person, which reads more naturally than a switch from "ninyi" to "wewe"; the same in 11:7-8. The meaning is unchanged.

source.text: κἀκεῖνος ἔσωθεν ἀποκριθεὶς εἴπῃ· Μή μοι κόπους πάρεχε· ἤδη ἡ θύρα κέκλεισται, καὶ τὰ παιδία μου μετ’ ἐμοῦ εἰς τὴν κοίτην εἰσίν· οὐ δύναμαι ἀναστὰς δοῦναί σοι.

records.literal_gloss: and that one from within answering will say, Not me troubles cause; already the door has been shut, and the children of me with me in the bed are; not I am able having risen to give to you.

en.L: and that one, answering from inside, will say, 'Do not cause me trouble; the door has already been shut, and my children are with me in bed; I am not able to get up and give [anything] to you'?
en.B: Would that friend call back from inside, 'Do not trouble me. The door is already shut for the night, and my children are in bed with me. I cannot get up now to hand you anything'?
en.R: Would your friend answer from inside the house, 'Do not bother me! The door is already locked. My children are in bed with me. I cannot get out of bed to give you anything'?

es.L: y aquel, respondiendo desde dentro, dirá: “No me causes molestias; ya está cerrada la puerta, y mis hijos están conmigo en la cama; no puedo levantarme a darte [algo]”?
es.B: ¿Le contestaría ese amigo desde dentro: “No me molestes. La puerta ya está cerrada por esta noche, y mis hijos están conmigo en la cama. Ahora no puedo levantarme a darte nada”?
es.R: ¿Le respondería su amigo desde dentro de la casa: “¡No me molestes! La puerta ya está cerrada con llave. Mis hijos están conmigo en la cama. No puedo levantarme para darte nada”?

sw.L: na yule, akijibu kutoka ndani, aseme, 'Usiniletee taabu; tayari mlango umefungwa, na wanangu wako nami kitandani; siwezi kuinuka kukupa [kitu]'?
sw.B: Je, rafiki huyo angejibu kutoka ndani, 'Usinisumbue. Mlango tayari umefungwa kwa usiku huu, na wanangu wamelala nami kitandani. Siwezi kuamka sasa nikupe chochote'?
sw.R: Je, rafiki yake angemjibu kutoka ndani ya nyumba, 'Usinisumbue! Mlango umeshafungwa. Watoto wangu wako kitandani pamoja nami. Siwezi kutoka kitandani nikupe chochote'?

decisions.choice: the door shut, the children in bed: the whole household is asleep
alternatives: a large house with many rooms
decisions.reason: In a small village house the family often slept together in one room. Getting up meant unbarring the door and waking the children.

decisions.choice: will answer: still part of the question begun in 11:5
decisions.reason: The sleeper's answer completes the question Jesus asked. The expected reply is that no friend would answer like this.

decisions.choice: a question: Would that friend ...? (B); Would your friend ...? (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the question plain at the point where the answer comes, since the start of the question is now some way back.

decisions.choice: for the night
decisions.reason: The door is shut because the household has gone to bed.

source.text: λέγω ὑμῖν, εἰ καὶ οὐ δώσει αὐτῷ ἀναστὰς διὰ τὸ εἶναι φίλον αὐτοῦ, διά γε τὴν ἀναίδειαν αὐτοῦ ἐγερθεὶς δώσει αὐτῷ ὅσων χρῄζει.

records.literal_gloss: I say to you, if even not he will give to him having risen because of the being friend of him, because of yet the shamelessness of him having risen he will give him as much as he needs.

en.L: I tell you, even if he will not get up and give to him because he is his friend, yet because of his shamelessness he will get up and give him as much as he needs.
en.B: I tell you, even if friendship is not enough to get him out of bed to give you the bread, your boldness in asking without shame will get him up, and he will give you as much as you need.
en.R: I tell you, being his friend may not be enough to make him get up and give you bread. But you were not ashamed to ask, even in the middle of the night. So he will get up and give you all you need.

es.L: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo: aunque no se levante a darle por ser su amigo, al menos por su desvergüenza se levantará y le dará cuanto necesite.
es.B: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo que, aunque la amistad no baste para sacarlo de la cama a darle el pan, el atrevimiento del que pide sin avergonzarse hará que se levante, y le dará todo lo que necesite.
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo que tal vez ser su amigo no baste para que se levante a darle pan. Pero el que pide no tuvo vergüenza de pedir, aun en medio de la noche. Por eso se levantará y le dará todo lo que necesite.

sw.L: Nawaambia, hata kama hataamka kumpa kwa sababu ni rafiki yake, lakini kwa sababu ya kutokuona haya kwake ataamka na kumpa kadiri anavyohitaji.
sw.B: Nawaambia, hata kama urafiki hautoshi kumtoa kitandani ampe mikate, ujasiri wa yule anayeomba bila kuona haya utamfanya aamke, naye atampa kila anachohitaji.
sw.R: Nawaambia, huenda kuwa rafiki yake hakutatosha kumfanya aamke ampe mikate. Lakini yule anayeomba hakuona haya kuomba, hata usiku wa manane. Kwa hiyo ataamka na kumpa kila anachohitaji.

decisions.choice: shamelessness: boldness that does not hold back for fear of shame
decisions.reason: The word means shamelessness, a lack of the restraint that shame would bring. Older renderings took it as persistence, but the man asks only once in the story. His boldness is in asking at all, at midnight, sure that his friend will help.

decisions.choice: his: the man who comes asking
alternatives: the man in bed, who gets up to avoid the shame of refusing a guest
decisions.reason: Several of the pronouns in this verse could refer to either man. Taken with 11:9-10, the point is the boldness of the one who asks. Some read it of the sleeper: he gets up so as not to be shamed for failing a neighbor's guest.

decisions.choice: the lesson: if a sleepy friend gives, God will surely give
alternatives: we must wear God down by asking
decisions.reason: The story argues from the lesser to the greater, as 11:13 does. God is not the reluctant friend; he is the one who gives far more readily.

decisions.choice: you, your (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek speaks of the asker in the third person. Balanced and Readable go on speaking to "you", as the story began in 11:5, so the reader can tell the two men apart.

decisions.choice: desvergüenza
decisions.reason: The word is a lack of shame, a boldness that does not hold back (meaning decision m1, uncertain), not simply persistence. Literal keeps the sharp word; Balanced and Readable say "atrevimiento" and "no tuvo vergüenza de pedir", as the English does.

decisions.choice: el atrevimiento del que pide (B); el que pide no tuvo vergüenza (R)
decisions.reason: The boldness is that of the man who comes asking (meaning decision m2, uncertain). The English Balanced and Readable say "your"; Spanish, which kept him in the third person from 11:5, names him "el que pide", which says the same thing plainly.

decisions.choice: kutokuona haya (L); ujasiri ... bila kuona haya (B); hakuona haya (R)
decisions.reason: The word is a lack of shame, a boldness that does not hold back (meaning decision m1, uncertain), not simply persistence, so Swahili speaks of not feeling shame ("kuona haya") rather than of going on asking.

decisions.choice: yule anayeomba
decisions.reason: The boldness is that of the man who comes asking (meaning decision m2, uncertain). The English Balanced and Readable say "your"; Swahili, which kept him in the third person from 11:5, names him "yule anayeomba", which says the same thing plainly.

source.text: Κἀγὼ ὑμῖν λέγω, αἰτεῖτε, καὶ δοθήσεται ὑμῖν· ζητεῖτε, καὶ εὑρήσετε· κρούετε, καὶ ἀνοιγήσεται ὑμῖν·

records.literal_gloss: And I to you say, ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you.

en.L: And I say to you, ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you.
en.B: So I tell you: ask, and God will give to you; search, and you will find; knock, and God will open the door for you.
en.R: So I tell you, keep asking God, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will give you what you ask for. Keep looking, and you will find. Keep knocking, and the door will be opened for you.

es.L: Y yo {{plural_you:les|os}} digo: {{plural_you:pidan|pedid}}, y se {{plural_you:les|os}} dará; {{plural_you:busquen|buscad}}, y {{plural_you:encontrarán|encontraréis}}; {{plural_you:toquen|tocad}} [a la puerta], y se {{plural_you:les|os}} abrirá.
es.B: Así que yo {{plural_you:les|os}} digo: {{plural_you:pidan|pedid}}, y Dios {{plural_you:les|os}} dará; {{plural_you:busquen|buscad}}, y {{plural_you:encontrarán|encontraréis}}; {{plural_you:llamen|llamad}} a la puerta, y Dios {{plural_you:les|os}} abrirá.
es.R: Por eso {{plural_you:les|os}} digo: {{plural_you:sigan|seguid}} pidiéndole a Dios, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} {{plural_you:les|os}} dará lo que {{plural_you:piden|pedís}}. {{plural_you:Sigan|Seguid}} buscando, y {{plural_you:encontrarán|encontraréis}}. {{plural_you:Sigan|Seguid}} llamando a la puerta, y se {{plural_you:les|os}} abrirá.

sw.L: Nami nawaambia: ombeni, na mtapewa; tafuteni, na mtapata; gongeni [mlango], na mtafunguliwa.
sw.B: Basi nawaambia: ombeni, na Mungu atawapa; tafuteni, na mtapata; bisheni hodi, na Mungu atawafungulia mlango.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo nawaambia, endeleeni kumwomba Mungu, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} atawapa mnachoomba. Endeleeni kutafuta, na mtapata. Endeleeni kubisha hodi, na mtafunguliwa mlango.

decisions.choice: it will be given, it will be opened: God is the giver
decisions.reason: The passive is a reverent way of speaking of what God does. 11:13 names the giver: the Father.

decisions.choice: ask, seek, knock: commands for a lasting practice
decisions.reason: The commands are in the present tense, which describes ongoing action: keep asking, keep seeking, keep knocking.

decisions.choice: knock: ask to be let in, as the friend did at the door
alternatives: a call to force the door
decisions.reason: The picture follows the story of the friend at the door (11:5-8).

decisions.choice: God will give ... God will open the door (B); God, and he will give (R); the door (B, R)
alternatives: it will be given ... it will be opened
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God as the giver, which the passive implies, and name the door that is opened.

decisions.choice: keep asking ... keep looking ... keep knocking
decisions.reason: Readable brings out the ongoing sense of the commands.

decisions.choice: toquen [a la puerta] (L); llamen a la puerta (B, R)
decisions.reason: The picture is of knocking to be let in, as the friend did at the door (meaning decision m3). Spanish "llamar" alone could be heard as calling out, so the door is named; Literal brackets it, as the English Literal leaves it out.

decisions.choice: gongeni [mlango] (L); bisheni hodi (B, R)
decisions.reason: The picture is of knocking to be let in, as the friend did at the door (meaning decision m3). "Kubisha hodi" is to knock and call at a door asking to come in, which is that picture; Literal keeps the bare verb with the door bracketed.

source.text: πᾶς γὰρ ὁ αἰτῶν λαμβάνει, καὶ ὁ ζητῶν εὑρίσκει, καὶ τῷ κρούοντι ἀνοιγήσεται.

records.literal_gloss: Everyone for the asking receives, and the [one] seeking finds, and to the [one] knocking it will be opened.

en.L: For everyone who asks receives, and the one who seeks finds, and to the one who knocks it will be opened.
en.B: For all who ask receive, all who search find, and all who knock have the door opened to them.
en.R: Everyone who asks will receive. Everyone who looks will find. And the door will be opened for everyone who knocks.

es.L: Porque todo el que pide recibe, y el que busca encuentra, y al que toca [a la puerta] se le abrirá.
es.B: Porque todos los que piden reciben, todos los que buscan encuentran, y a todos los que llaman a la puerta se les abrirá.
es.R: Todo el que pide recibirá. Todo el que busca encontrará. Y a todo el que llama a la puerta se le abrirá.

sw.L: Kwa maana kila anayeomba hupokea, na anayetafuta hupata, na anayegonga [mlango] atafunguliwa.
sw.B: Kwa maana wote wanaoomba hupokea, wote wanaotafuta hupata, na wote wanaobisha hodi watafunguliwa mlango.
sw.R: Kila mtu anayeomba atapokea. Kila anayetafuta atapata. Na kila anayebisha hodi atafunguliwa mlango.

decisions.choice: for: the reason to ask
decisions.reason: The promise holds for everyone who asks, and that is why the disciples should ask.

decisions.choice: it will be opened: future, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: it is opened: present, the reading of some manuscripts
decisions.reason: Manuscripts differ between the future and the present tense here. The meaning is the same. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: three short sentences
decisions.reason: Readable gives each promise its own sentence.

decisions.choice: the door
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the door that is opened, as in 11:9.

source.text: τίνα δὲ ἐξ ὑμῶν τὸν πατέρα αἰτήσει ὁ υἱὸς ἰχθύν, καὶ ἀντὶ ἰχθύος ὄφιν αὐτῷ ἐπιδώσει;

records.literal_gloss: Which now of you the father will ask the son for a fish, and instead of a fish a snake to him will give?

en.L: And which father among you, [if his] son asks for a fish, will give him a snake instead of a fish?
en.B: Is there a father among you who would hand his son a snake when the boy asked for a fish?
en.R: You fathers, suppose your son asks you for a fish. Would you give him a snake instead?

es.L: ¿Y a qué padre de entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} le pedirá el hijo un pez, y en lugar del pez le dará una serpiente?
es.B: ¿Hay entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} algún padre que, si su hijo le pide un pescado, le dé una serpiente?
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}}, padres: {{plural_you:supongan|suponed}} que {{plural_you:su hijo les|vuestro hijo os}} pide un pescado. ¿Le {{plural_you:darían|daríais}} una serpiente en vez del pescado?

sw.L: Na ni baba yupi miongoni mwenu ambaye mwanawe atamwomba samaki, naye badala ya samaki atampa nyoka?
sw.B: Je, yuko baba miongoni mwenu ambaye mwanawe akimwomba samaki, atampa nyoka?
sw.R: Ninyi akina baba, tuseme mtoto wenu anawaomba samaki. Je, mngempa nyoka badala yake?

decisions.choice: a fish ... a snake: the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: "bread ... a stone" first, then the fish and the snake, as in many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add a first question, about a son asking for bread and being given a stone, from Matthew 7:9. Several early manuscripts lack it, and it is likely to have come in from Matthew. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: a question expecting the answer "no"
decisions.reason: No father would do such a thing. Each pair puts something harmful in place of the food the child asked for.

decisions.choice: You fathers, suppose ... Would you ...?
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the question into two short sentences.

source.text: ἢ καὶ αἰτήσει ᾠόν, ἐπιδώσει αὐτῷ σκορπίον;

records.literal_gloss: Or also he will ask for an egg, will he give to him a scorpion?

en.L: Or also [if] he asks for an egg, will [he] give him a scorpion?
en.B: Or if he asked for an egg, would he give him a scorpion?
en.R: Or if he asks for an egg, would you give him a scorpion?

es.L: ¿O también [si] pide un huevo, le dará un escorpión?
es.B: ¿O si le pidiera un huevo, le daría un escorpión?
es.R: ¿O si {{plural_you:les|os}} pide un huevo, le {{plural_you:darían|daríais}} un escorpión?

sw.L: Au pia atamwomba yai, naye atampa nge?
sw.B: Au akimwomba yai, je, angempa nge?
sw.R: Au akiwaomba yai, je, mngempa nge?

decisions.choice: scorpion: a small creature with a painful, poisonous sting
decisions.reason: Scorpions were common in the land and in the wilderness (Deuteronomy 8:15; Luke 10:19).

decisions.choice: would you give
decisions.reason: Readable keeps speaking to the fathers as "you", as in 11:11.

source.text: εἰ οὖν ὑμεῖς πονηροὶ ὑπάρχοντες οἴδατε δόματα ἀγαθὰ διδόναι τοῖς τέκνοις ὑμῶν, πόσῳ μᾶλλον ὁ πατὴρ ὁ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ δώσει πνεῦμα ἅγιον τοῖς αἰτοῦσιν αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: If therefore you evil being know gifts good to give to the children of you, how much more the Father the from heaven will give [the] Spirit Holy to those asking him.

en.L: If then you, being evil, know [how] to give good gifts to your children, how much more will the Father from heaven give [the] Holy Spirit to those who ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!"
en.B: You are evil, and yet you know how to give your children good gifts. Then how much more will the Father in heaven give the Holy Spirit to those who ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!"
en.R: Even though you are evil, you know how to give good things to your children. So the Father in heaven will be much more ready to give the Holy Spirit to those who ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!"

es.L: Si, pues, {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, siendo malos, {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} dar buenos regalos a {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} hijos, ¡cuánto más el Padre del cielo dará [el] Espíritu Santo a los que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} piden!».
es.B: {{plural_you:Ustedes son|Vosotros sois}} malos, y aun así {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} dar buenos regalos a {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} hijos. Entonces, ¡cuánto más dará el Padre que está en el cielo el Espíritu Santo a quienes {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} piden!».
es.R: Aunque {{plural_you:son|sois}} malos, {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} dar cosas buenas a {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} hijos. Pues el Padre que está en el cielo está mucho más dispuesto a dar el Espíritu Santo a los que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} piden».

sw.L: Basi kama ninyi, ingawa ni waovu, mnajua kuwapa watoto wenu zawadi nzuri, si zaidi sana Baba wa kutoka mbinguni atawapa Roho Mtakatifu wale wanaomwomba!"
sw.B: Ninyi ni waovu, hata hivyo mnajua kuwapa watoto wenu zawadi nzuri. Basi si zaidi sana kwamba Baba aliye mbinguni atawapa Roho Mtakatifu wale wanaomwomba!"
sw.R: Ingawa ninyi ni waovu, mnajua kuwapa watoto wenu vitu vizuri. Basi Baba aliye mbinguni yuko tayari zaidi sana kuwapa Roho Mtakatifu wale wanaomwomba!"

decisions.choice: how much more: an argument from the lesser to the greater
decisions.reason: If human fathers, sinful as they are, give their children good things, God the Father will surely give his best gift.

decisions.choice: the Holy Spirit: the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Most manuscripts, the oldest among them, read "the Holy Spirit". A few have "good things", the wording of Matthew 7:11, or similar phrases. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the Holy Spirit: the gift the Father gives
decisions.reason: John promised that the one coming would baptize with the Holy Spirit (3:16). Jesus later promises the Spirit as the Father's gift (24:49; Acts 1:4-5; 2:33).

decisions.choice: the Father from heaven: the heavenly Father
alternatives: the Father will give from heaven
decisions.reason: The words "from heaven" can describe the Father, as "heavenly" does, or say where the gift comes from. Either way the giver is the Father in heaven.

decisions.choice: evil: sinful, compared with God's goodness
decisions.reason: Jesus is not singling out especially bad fathers. Compared with God, all people are sinful (18:19).

decisions.choice: a statement first, then the conclusion
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the fact about human fathers first, which makes the argument easier to follow.

source.text: Καὶ ἦν ἐκβάλλων δαιμόνιον κωφόν· ἐγένετο δὲ τοῦ δαιμονίου ἐξελθόντος ἐλάλησεν ὁ κωφός.

records.literal_gloss: And he was casting out a demon mute; it came about then the demon having gone out spoke the mute.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was casting out a demon [that was] mute; and it happened, when the demon had gone out, the mute [man] spoke.
en.B: Jesus was driving out a demon that had left a man unable to speak. Once the demon was gone, the man spoke.
en.R: Jesus was forcing a demon to come out of a man. The demon had made the man unable to talk. When the demon came out, the man began to speak.

es.L: Y estaba echando fuera un demonio [que era] mudo; y sucedió que, cuando el demonio salió, el mudo habló.
es.B: Jesús estaba expulsando un demonio que había dejado mudo a un hombre. Cuando el demonio salió, el hombre habló.
es.R: Jesús estaba haciendo salir un demonio de un hombre. El demonio había dejado al hombre sin poder hablar. Cuando el demonio salió, el hombre comenzó a hablar.

sw.L: Naye alikuwa akifukuza pepo [aliyekuwa] bubu; na pepo alipotoka, ikawa yule bubu akaongea.
sw.B: Yesu alikuwa akimfukuza pepo aliyekuwa amemfanya mtu mmoja asiweze kusema. Pepo alipotoka, mtu huyo akasema.
sw.R: Yesu alikuwa akimlazimisha pepo amtoke mtu mmoja. Pepo huyo alikuwa amemfanya mtu huyo asiweze kuongea. Pepo alipotoka, mtu huyo akaanza kuongea.

decisions.choice: a mute demon: a demon that made the man unable to speak
alternatives: a demon that could not speak
decisions.reason: The demon is named by what it did to the man. The word can mean deaf as well as mute (7:22); here the man speaks once he is free.

decisions.choice: Jesus; a man
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus at the start of a new section and say that the demon was in a man.

decisions.choice: demonio
decisions.reason: As the term sheet settles for the whole New Testament, "demonio" names these spirits; "diablo" is kept for Satan himself (11:18).

decisions.choice: pepo
decisions.reason: As the term sheet settles for the whole New Testament, "pepo" names these spirits; "Shetani" is kept for Satan himself (11:18).

source.text: καὶ ἐθαύμασαν οἱ ὄχλοι·

records.literal_gloss: And marveled the crowds.

en.L: And the crowds marveled.
en.B: The crowds were amazed.
en.R: The people were amazed.

es.L: Y se maravillaron las multitudes.
es.B: Las multitudes quedaron asombradas.
es.R: La gente quedó asombrada.

sw.L: Na makutano wakastaajabu.
sw.B: Makutano wakashangaa.
sw.R: Watu wakashangaa.

decisions.choice: The people
decisions.reason: Readable says "the people" for the crowds who watched.

source.text: τινὲς δὲ ἐξ αὐτῶν εἶπον· Ἐν Βεελζεβοὺλ τῷ ἄρχοντι τῶν δαιμονίων ἐκβάλλει τὰ δαιμόνια·

records.literal_gloss: Some then of them said, By Beelzebul the ruler of the demons he casts out the demons;

en.L: But some of them said, "By Beelzebul, the ruler of the demons, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} casts out the demons."
en.B: But some of them said, "It is by Beelzebul, the ruler of the demons, that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} drives out the demons."
en.R: But some of the people said, "Beelzebul, the ruler of the demons, gives {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} power to force demons out."

es.L: Pero algunos de ellos dijeron: «Por Beelzebul, el príncipe de los demonios, echa fuera los demonios».
es.B: Pero algunos de ellos dijeron: «Expulsa los demonios por medio de Beelzebul, el jefe de los demonios».
es.R: Pero algunas personas decían: «Beelzebul, el jefe de los demonios, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} da poder para hacer salir a los demonios».

sw.L: Lakini baadhi yao wakasema, "Kwa Beelzebuli, mkuu wa pepo, anawatoa pepo."
sw.B: Lakini baadhi yao wakasema, "Anawafukuza pepo kwa uwezo wa Beelzebuli, mkuu wa pepo."
sw.R: Lakini baadhi ya watu wakasema, "Beelzebuli, mtawala wa pepo, ndiye anayempa nguvu za kuwafukuza pepo."

decisions.choice: Beelzebul, the ruler of the demons: a name for Satan
decisions.reason: Jesus answers the charge by speaking of Satan (11:18), so the name stands for him. It recalls Baal-zebub, a god of the Philistine city of Ekron (2 Kings 1:2-3), a name that means "lord of flies". The form "zebul" may mean a lofty house, which would fit the pictures of the kingdom and the house in 11:17-22.

decisions.choice: Beelzebul: the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: Beelzebub, the reading of the old Latin and Syriac versions
Beezebul, the reading of a few early manuscripts
decisions.reason: Greek manuscripts mostly read Beelzebul; a few early ones have Beezebul. The form Beelzebub, familiar from older translations, comes from the ancient versions and matches the name in 2 Kings 1:2. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: by: by the power of
decisions.reason: They do not deny that the demon has gone. They claim that the power behind Jesus is Satan's.

decisions.choice: Beelzebul ... gives him power to force demons out
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "by Beelzebul" means.

source.text: ἕτεροι δὲ πειράζοντες σημεῖον ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἐζήτουν παρ’ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Others then testing a sign from heaven were seeking from him.

en.L: And others, testing [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}], were seeking from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a sign from heaven.
en.B: Others, wanting to test {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, kept asking {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for a sign from heaven.
en.R: Others wanted to test Jesus. They asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to show them a sign from heaven to prove that God had sent {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Y otros, para poner[lo] a prueba, buscaban de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} una señal del cielo.
es.B: Otros, que querían ponerlo a prueba, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} seguían pidiendo una señal del cielo.
es.R: Otros querían poner a prueba a Jesús. Le pidieron que les mostrara una señal del cielo para probar que Dios {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} había enviado.

sw.L: Na wengine, wakimjaribu, walikuwa wakitafuta {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}} ishara kutoka mbinguni.
sw.B: Wengine, wakitaka kumjaribu, waliendelea kumwomba ishara kutoka mbinguni.
sw.R: Wengine walitaka kumjaribu Yesu. Wakamwomba awaonyeshe ishara kutoka mbinguni ili kuthibitisha kwamba Mungu ndiye aliyemtuma.

decisions.choice: sign: a visible act from God that would prove Jesus' claims
decisions.reason: They had just seen a demon driven out, yet they ask for more: a proof from heaven that could not be doubted. Jesus answers in 11:29-30.

decisions.choice: from heaven: from God
decisions.reason: Heaven stands for God. They want a sign that God himself gives, though some may have pictured a wonder in the sky.

decisions.choice: testing: putting him to the test, hoping to trap him
decisions.reason: The word is used of the devil's testing (4:2, 12) and of the expert in the law who tested Jesus (10:25).

decisions.choice: to prove that God had sent him
decisions.reason: Readable says what such a sign from heaven was meant to show.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus where the Greek has a pronoun or leaves the subject unstated, so young readers can follow who is acting.

decisions.choice: señal
decisions.reason: They ask for proof from God (meaning decision m1), so "señal" is kept, as in John and Matthew, rather than "milagro", which would be only a wonder.

decisions.choice: ishara
decisions.reason: They ask for proof from God (meaning decision m1), so "ishara" (sign) is kept, as in John and Matthew, rather than "muujiza" (miracle), which would be only a wonder.

source.text: αὐτὸς δὲ εἰδὼς αὐτῶν τὰ διανοήματα εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Πᾶσα βασιλεία ἐφ’ ἑαυτὴν διαμερισθεῖσα ἐρημοῦται, καὶ οἶκος ἐπὶ οἶκον πίπτει.

records.literal_gloss: He now knowing of them the thoughts said to them, Every kingdom against itself having been divided is laid waste, and house against house falls.

en.L: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}, knowing their thoughts, said to them, "Every kingdom divided against itself is laid waste, and house falls upon house.
en.B: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} knew what they were thinking, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "If a kingdom is torn apart by its own people, it is laid waste, and its houses fall one upon another.
en.R: Jesus knew what they were thinking. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "If the people of a kingdom fight against each other, that kingdom will be destroyed. Its houses will fall down on top of each other.

es.L: Pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, conociendo sus pensamientos, les dijo: «Todo reino dividido contra sí mismo queda devastado, y casa cae sobre casa.
es.B: Pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} sabía lo que estaban pensando, y les dijo: «Si un reino es desgarrado por su propia gente, queda en ruinas, y sus casas se derrumban unas sobre otras.
es.R: Jesús sabía lo que estaban pensando. Por eso les dijo: «Si la gente de un reino pelea entre sí, ese reino será destruido. Sus casas se caerán unas encima de otras.

sw.L: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}, akiyajua mawazo yao, akawaambia, "Kila ufalme uliogawanyika dhidi yake wenyewe hufanywa ukiwa, na nyumba huangukia nyumba.
sw.B: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} aliyajua mawazo yao, akawaambia, "Ufalme ukisambaratishwa na watu wake wenyewe, huharibiwa, na nyumba zake huangukiana.
sw.R: Yesu alijua walichokuwa wakifikiri. Kwa hiyo akawaambia, "Watu wa ufalme mmoja wakipigana wao kwa wao, ufalme huo utaangamizwa. Nyumba zake zitaangukiana.

decisions.choice: house falls upon house: in the ruin of a divided kingdom, houses collapse on one another
alternatives: a household divided against itself falls
decisions.reason: The phrase is short and can be read two ways. It may go on picturing the kingdom laid waste, its houses falling in heaps. Or it may be a second example, a divided household that falls, as in Mark 3:25 and Matthew 12:25.

decisions.choice: knowing their thoughts: Jesus knows what they think
decisions.reason: Luke shows Jesus knowing people's thoughts (5:22; 6:8; 9:47).

decisions.choice: is laid waste: is brought to ruin
decisions.reason: The word is used of a land or city left in ruins.

decisions.choice: torn apart by its own people (B); the people of a kingdom fight against each other (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what it means for a kingdom to be divided against itself.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus where the Greek has a pronoun or leaves the subject unstated, so young readers can follow who is acting.

source.text: εἰ δὲ καὶ ὁ Σατανᾶς ἐφ’ ἑαυτὸν διεμερίσθη, πῶς σταθήσεται ἡ βασιλεία αὐτοῦ;

records.literal_gloss: If now also the Satan against himself was divided, how will stand the kingdom of him?

en.L: And if Satan also is divided against himself, how will his kingdom stand?
en.B: If Satan too is split against himself, how can his kingdom last?
en.R: In the same way, if Satan is fighting against himself, how can his kingdom last?

es.L: Y si también Satanás está dividido contra sí mismo, ¿cómo se mantendrá su reino?
es.B: Si también Satanás está dividido contra sí mismo, ¿cómo podrá durar su reino?
es.R: De la misma manera, si Satanás pelea contra sí mismo, ¿cómo puede durar su reino?

sw.L: Na kama Shetani naye amegawanyika dhidi yake mwenyewe, ufalme wake utasimamaje?
sw.B: Ikiwa Shetani naye amegawanyika dhidi yake mwenyewe, ufalme wake utadumuje?
sw.R: Vivyo hivyo, kama Shetani anajipiga vita mwenyewe, ufalme wake utadumuje?

decisions.choice: Satan: the enemy of God and his people, the devil
decisions.reason: Satan is the devil who tested Jesus (4:1-13). Jesus treats Beelzebul (11:15) as another name for him.

decisions.choice: how will his kingdom stand: a question expecting the answer that it cannot
decisions.reason: If Satan were driving out his own demons he would be destroying his own rule. The charge makes no sense.

decisions.choice: In the same way
decisions.reason: Readable shows how Satan's case follows from the picture of the kingdom in 11:17.

source.text: ὅτι λέγετε ἐν Βεελζεβοὺλ ἐκβάλλειν με τὰ δαιμόνια.

records.literal_gloss: For you say by Beelzebul cast out I the demons.

en.L: For you say that I cast out the demons by Beelzebul.
en.B: Yet that is what you are saying: that I drive out the demons by Beelzebul.
en.R: And yet you say that Beelzebul gives {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} power to force demons out.

es.L: Porque {{plural_you:dicen|decís}} que por Beelzebul echo yo fuera los demonios.
es.B: Y eso es precisamente lo que {{plural_you:dicen|decís}}: que yo expulso los demonios por Beelzebul.
es.R: Y sin embargo {{plural_you:ustedes dicen|vosotros decís}} que Beelzebul {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} da poder para hacer salir a los demonios.

sw.L: Kwa sababu mnasema kwamba {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} natoa pepo kwa Beelzebuli.
sw.B: Na hivyo ndivyo mnavyosema: kwamba nawafukuza pepo kwa Beelzebuli.
sw.R: Lakini mnasema kwamba Beelzebuli ndiye anayenipa nguvu za kuwafukuza pepo.

decisions.choice: for: why Jesus speaks of Satan divided against himself
decisions.reason: Jesus explains why he has raised the question: their charge would mean that Satan is fighting himself.

decisions.choice: Yet that is what you are saying (B); And yet you say (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out the link with the question before it.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}
decisions.reason: As in John and Matthew: when Jesus speaks of himself, the free pronoun "mimi" takes the deity_pronoun setting in Swahili, though the English "I" has none. The pronouns marked inside the verb (natoa, nawafukuza) are written plain. The same in 11:19.

source.text: εἰ δὲ ἐγὼ ἐν Βεελζεβοὺλ ἐκβάλλω τὰ δαιμόνια, οἱ υἱοὶ ὑμῶν ἐν τίνι ἐκβάλλουσιν;

records.literal_gloss: If now I by Beelzebul cast out the demons, the sons of you by whom do they cast out?

en.L: And if I cast out the demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons cast [them] out?
en.B: And if I drive out the demons by Beelzebul, by whose power do your own people drive them out?
en.R: If Beelzebul gives {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} power to force demons out, then who gives your own followers power to force them out?

es.L: Y si yo echo fuera los demonios por Beelzebul, ¿{{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} hijos por quién [los] echan fuera?
es.B: Y si yo expulso los demonios por Beelzebul, ¿por el poder de quién los expulsa {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} propia gente?
es.R: Si Beelzebul {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} da poder para hacer salir a los demonios, entonces, ¿quién les da poder a {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} propios seguidores para hacerlos salir?

sw.L: Na ikiwa {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} natoa pepo kwa Beelzebuli, wana wenu wao huwatoa kwa nani?
sw.B: Na kama {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} nawafukuza pepo kwa Beelzebuli, watu wenu wenyewe huwafukuza kwa uwezo wa nani?
sw.R: Kama Beelzebuli ndiye anayenipa nguvu za kuwafukuza pepo, basi ni nani anayewapa wafuasi wenu wenyewe nguvu za kuwafukuza?

decisions.choice: your sons: your own followers, people of your own group
decisions.reason: "Sons" can mean followers or members of a group. Some Jews of the time also drove out demons (compare Acts 19:13-14). If Jesus' power came from Satan, so would theirs.

decisions.choice: if I cast out ... by Beelzebul: supposed for the sake of argument
decisions.reason: Jesus takes up their claim to show where it leads.

decisions.choice: your own people (B); your own followers (R)
decisions.reason: "Your sons" would suggest their children. Balanced and Readable say what is meant.

source.text: διὰ τοῦτο αὐτοὶ ὑμῶν κριταὶ ἔσονται.

records.literal_gloss: Because of this they of you judges will be.

en.L: Because of this they will be your judges.
en.B: So they themselves will be the ones to judge you.
en.R: So your own followers will show that you are wrong.

es.L: Por esto, ellos serán {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} jueces.
es.B: Así que ellos mismos serán quienes {{plural_you:los|os}} juzguen.
es.R: Así que {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} propios seguidores demostrarán que {{plural_you:están|estáis}} equivocados.

sw.L: Kwa sababu hiyo, wao watakuwa waamuzi wenu.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo wao wenyewe ndio watakaowahukumu.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo wafuasi wenu wenyewe wataonyesha kwamba mmekosea.

decisions.choice: they will be your judges: their own work shows the charge to be false
alternatives: they will judge you on the last day
decisions.reason: The work of their own people shows that driving out demons is not Satan's work, so it judges the accusers. Some also see a reference to the final judgment.

decisions.choice: will show that you are wrong
decisions.reason: Readable says what this judging consists of here.

source.text: εἰ δὲ ἐν δακτύλῳ θεοῦ ἐκβάλλω τὰ δαιμόνια, ἄρα ἔφθασεν ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: If however by [the] finger of God I cast out the demons, then has come upon you the kingdom of God.

en.L: But if I cast out the demons by [the] finger of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.
en.B: But suppose it is by God's finger that I drive the demons out. Then the kingdom of God has already reached you.
en.R: But suppose I force demons out by the finger of God, that is, by God's own power. Then the kingdom of God has already come to you.

es.L: Pero si echo fuera los demonios por [el] dedo de Dios, entonces el reino de Dios ha llegado sobre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.B: Pero {{plural_you:supongan|suponed}} que expulso los demonios por el dedo de Dios. Entonces el reino de Dios ya ha llegado hasta {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.R: Pero {{plural_you:supongan|suponed}} que hago salir a los demonios por el dedo de Dios, es decir, por el poder de Dios mismo. Entonces el reino de Dios ya ha llegado a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

sw.L: Lakini kama natoa pepo kwa kidole cha Mungu, basi ufalme wa Mungu umekuja juu yenu.
sw.B: Lakini tuseme nawafukuza pepo kwa kidole cha Mungu. Basi ufalme wa Mungu tayari umewafikia.
sw.R: Lakini tuseme nawafukuza pepo kwa kidole cha Mungu, yaani kwa nguvu za Mungu mwenyewe. Basi ufalme wa Mungu tayari umekuja kwenu.

decisions.choice: the finger of God: Exodus 8:19
alternatives: a figure of speech with no background
decisions.reason: When the magicians of Egypt could not match the plague of gnats, they told Pharaoh that it was the finger of God. The tablets of the law were written by the finger of God (Exodus 31:18). Jesus' power over demons is the same power God showed at the exodus. Matthew 12:28 has "the Spirit of God".

decisions.choice: has come upon you: has arrived, has reached you
decisions.reason: The verb means to arrive or reach. God's rule is already present in Jesus' work of setting people free.

decisions.choice: if: a condition Jesus means as true
decisions.reason: This is the real explanation of his power, set against the false one in 11:19.

decisions.choice: suppose ... Then ...
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable break the condition into two sentences.

decisions.choice: that is, by God's own power
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of God's finger.

source.text: ὅταν ὁ ἰσχυρὸς καθωπλισμένος φυλάσσῃ τὴν ἑαυτοῦ αὐλήν, ἐν εἰρήνῃ ἐστὶν τὰ ὑπάρχοντα αὐτοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: When the strong [man] being fully armed guards the his own courtyard, in peace are the possessions of him;

en.L: When the strong [man], fully armed, guards his own courtyard, his possessions are in peace.
en.B: As long as a strong man keeps guard over his own palace with all his weapons, his goods are left in peace.
en.R: When a strong man guards his own house with all his weapons, his things are left in peace.

es.L: Cuando el [hombre] fuerte, bien armado, guarda su propio patio, sus posesiones están en paz.
es.B: Mientras un hombre fuerte, con todas sus armas, vigila su propio palacio, sus bienes quedan en paz.
es.R: Cuando un hombre fuerte cuida su propia casa con todas sus armas, sus cosas están seguras.

sw.L: Mtu mwenye nguvu aliyejihami kikamilifu anapolinda ua wake mwenyewe, mali zake ziko katika amani.
sw.B: Maadamu mtu mwenye nguvu analinda jumba lake akiwa na silaha zake zote, mali zake hukaa salama.
sw.R: Mtu mwenye nguvu anapolinda nyumba yake mwenyewe akiwa na silaha zake zote, vitu vyake hubaki salama.

decisions.choice: in peace: safe and undisturbed
decisions.reason: The word here means safety: no one touches his goods.

decisions.choice: courtyard: a house built around a courtyard, a palace
decisions.reason: The word first meant a courtyard, then a large house or palace built around one.

decisions.choice: the strong man: Satan, who holds people in his power
decisions.reason: The picture explains the driving out of demons. Satan guards what he holds, but a stronger one has come (11:22).

decisions.choice: palace (B); house (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the building the courtyard belongs to.

source.text: ἐπὰν δὲ ἰσχυρότερος αὐτοῦ ἐπελθὼν νικήσῃ αὐτόν, τὴν πανοπλίαν αὐτοῦ αἴρει ἐφ’ ᾗ ἐπεποίθει, καὶ τὰ σκῦλα αὐτοῦ διαδίδωσιν.

records.literal_gloss: when however one stronger than he having come upon [him] overcomes him, the full armor of him he takes away in which he had trusted, and the spoils of him he divides.

en.L: but when one stronger than he comes upon [him and] overcomes him, he takes away his full armor in which he had trusted, and divides his spoils.
en.B: But then a man stronger than he is comes against him and wins the fight. He strips away all the armor the strong man was counting on, and shares out the goods he has seized.
en.R: But then someone stronger comes and attacks him and beats him. He takes away all the weapons and armor the strong man trusted. Then he gives away the things he took from him.

es.L: pero cuando uno más fuerte que él viene sobre [él y] lo vence, le quita la armadura completa en la que confiaba, y reparte su botín.
es.B: Pero entonces llega contra él uno más fuerte que él y lo vence. Le quita toda la armadura en la que confiaba el hombre fuerte, y reparte los bienes que le ha arrebatado.
es.R: Pero después llega alguien más fuerte, lo ataca y lo vence. Le quita todas las armas y la armadura en que el hombre fuerte confiaba. Luego reparte lo que le quitó.

sw.L: lakini mwenye nguvu kuliko yeye anapomjia [na] kumshinda, humnyang'anya silaha zake zote alizozitegemea, na kugawa mateka yake.
sw.B: Lakini kisha mtu mwenye nguvu zaidi yake anakuja dhidi yake na kumshinda. Anamnyang'anya silaha zote ambazo yule mwenye nguvu alizitegemea, na kugawa mali aliyoiteka.
sw.R: Lakini kisha mtu mwenye nguvu zaidi anakuja, anamshambulia na kumshinda. Anamnyang'anya silaha zote ambazo yule mwenye nguvu alizitumainia. Kisha anagawa vitu alivyomnyang'anya.

decisions.choice: one stronger: Jesus, the stronger one John promised
decisions.reason: John said that one stronger than he would come (3:16), using the same word. Jesus' power over the demons shows that he has overcome Satan.

decisions.choice: divides his spoils: Isaiah 49:24-25; 53:12
decisions.reason: Isaiah asks whether the prey can be taken from the mighty, and the LORD answers that it will be. The LORD's servant divides the spoil with the strong. The people Satan held are set free.

decisions.choice: full armor: all his weapons and armor
decisions.reason: The word means a soldier's full equipment for battle.

decisions.choice: two or three sentences
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable tell the struggle step by step, and name "the strong man" so the reader can tell the two apart.

source.text: ὁ μὴ ὢν μετ’ ἐμοῦ κατ’ ἐμοῦ ἐστιν, καὶ ὁ μὴ συνάγων μετ’ ἐμοῦ σκορπίζει.

records.literal_gloss: The [one] not being with me against me is, and the [one] not gathering with me scatters.

en.L: The one who is not with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and the one who does not gather with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} scatters.
en.B: Anyone who does not stand with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} stands against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and anyone who does not help {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} gather is scattering.
en.R: If you are not with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, you are against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. If you do not help {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} gather, you are scattering.

es.L: El que no está conmigo está contra {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, y el que no recoge conmigo dispersa.
es.B: Todo el que no se pone de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} lado está en contra de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, y todo el que no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ayuda a recoger está desparramando.
es.R: Si no estás conmigo, estás en contra de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. Si no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ayudas a recoger, estás dispersando.

sw.L: Asiye pamoja {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} yuko dhidi {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, na asiyekusanya pamoja {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} anatawanya.
sw.B: Mtu yeyote asiyesimama upande {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} anasimama kinyume {{deity_pronoun:changu|Changu}}, na mtu yeyote asiyenisaidia kukusanya anatawanya.
sw.R: Kama hauko pamoja {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}}, uko kinyume {{deity_pronoun:changu|Changu}}. Kama husaidii kukusanya pamoja {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}}, unatawanya.

decisions.choice: gather, scatter: a picture of gathering a flock
decisions.reason: God promised to gather his scattered flock (Ezekiel 34:12-13). Jesus is gathering God's people; whoever does not join in works against it.

decisions.choice: no neutral ground
decisions.reason: In 9:50 Jesus told the disciples not to stop a man who drove out demons in his name: whoever is not against them is for them. Here he speaks of each person's own stand toward him. The two sayings answer different situations.

decisions.choice: If you ...
decisions.reason: Readable speaks to the hearer directly.

decisions.choice: conmigo, with no span
decisions.reason: "Conmigo" is one word, "with me", and is written plain, as in John and Matthew; the other pronouns for Jesus (mí, mi, me) take the deity_pronoun setting as the English does.

source.text: Ὅταν τὸ ἀκάθαρτον πνεῦμα ἐξέλθῃ ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου, διέρχεται δι’ ἀνύδρων τόπων ζητοῦν ἀνάπαυσιν, καὶ μὴ εὑρίσκον λέγει· Ὑποστρέψω εἰς τὸν οἶκόν μου ὅθεν ἐξῆλθον·

records.literal_gloss: When the unclean spirit goes out from the man, it passes through waterless places seeking rest, and not finding it says, I will return to the house of me from where I came out;

en.L: When the unclean spirit has gone out from the {{gender:person|man}}, it passes through waterless places seeking rest, and not finding [any], it says, 'I will return to my house from which I came out.'
en.B: When an unclean spirit has left a {{gender:person|man}}, it wanders through dry, empty places looking for a place to rest. When it finds none, it says, 'I will go back to my house, where I came from.'
en.R: When an evil spirit comes out of someone, it travels through the desert looking for a place to rest. But it does not find one. So it says, 'I will go back to the house I came from.'

es.L: Cuando el espíritu impuro sale {{gender:de la persona|del hombre}}, pasa por lugares sin agua buscando descanso, y como no [lo] encuentra, dice: “Volveré a mi casa, de donde salí”.
es.B: Cuando un espíritu impuro ha salido de {{gender:una persona|un hombre}}, anda por lugares secos y desiertos buscando dónde descansar. Como no lo encuentra, dice: “Volveré a mi casa, de donde salí”.
es.R: Cuando un espíritu maligno sale de alguien, recorre el desierto buscando un lugar para descansar. Pero no lo encuentra. Entonces dice: “Volveré a la casa de donde salí”.

sw.L: Pepo mchafu akishamtoka mtu, hutembea katika maeneo yasiyo na maji akitafuta pumziko; na akikosa, husema, 'Nitarejea kwenye nyumba yangu, nilikotoka.'
sw.B: Pepo mchafu akimwacha mtu, huzurura katika nchi kavu isiyo na watu akitafuta mahali pa kupumzika. Asipopata, husema, 'Nitarudi kwenye nyumba yangu, kule nilikotoka.'
sw.R: Pepo mbaya anapomtoka mtu, husafiri jangwani akitafuta mahali pa kupumzika. Lakini hapapati. Kwa hiyo husema, 'Nitarudi kwenye nyumba niliyotoka.'

decisions.choice: unclean spirit: an evil spirit, a demon
alternatives: a spirit that is physically dirty
decisions.reason: Luke uses "unclean spirit" and "demon" for the same beings (4:33; 8:27-29).

decisions.choice: waterless places: the desert, thought of as a haunt of evil spirits
decisions.reason: The desert was pictured as the home of wild creatures and spirits (Isaiah 34:14; Luke 8:29).

decisions.choice: my house: the person the spirit had lived in
decisions.reason: The spirit speaks of the person it left as its home.

decisions.choice: evil spirit (R); unclean spirit (L, B)
decisions.reason: "Unclean" here means evil, not dirty. Readable says "evil", as in 4:33.

decisions.choice: person as the default, man as the alternative
decisions.reason: The word means a human being, man or woman. Readable says "someone".

decisions.choice: espíritu impuro (L, B); espíritu maligno (R)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet settles for the whole New Testament: "impuro" says that the spirit is opposed to God's holiness (meaning decision m1); Readable uses the plainer "maligno", as the English Readable says "evil".

decisions.choice: {{gender:de la persona|del hombre}} (L); {{gender:una persona|un hombre}} (B)
decisions.reason: As the English: the Greek word is "man" in the sense of any human being, so the inclusive "persona" is the default and "hombre" the traditional alternative; the span takes in the words that agree. The same in 11:26.

decisions.choice: pepo mchafu (L, B); pepo mbaya (R)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet settles for the whole New Testament: "mchafu" (unclean) says that the spirit is opposed to God's holiness (meaning decision m1); Readable uses the plainer "mbaya", as the English Readable says "evil".

decisions.choice: mtu, with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English offers "man" as the traditional alternative to "person" here and in 11:26. "Mtu" already means anyone, man or woman, so Swahili needs no span; "mwanamume" would mean a male only.

source.text: καὶ ἐλθὸν εὑρίσκει σεσαρωμένον καὶ κεκοσμημένον.

records.literal_gloss: And having come it finds swept and put in order.

en.L: And having come, it finds [it] swept and put in order.
en.B: It arrives and finds the house swept and tidied.
en.R: When it gets there, it finds that the house has been swept clean and everything is neat.

es.L: Y al llegar, [la] encuentra barrida y arreglada.
es.B: Llega y encuentra la casa barrida y ordenada.
es.R: Cuando llega, encuentra que la casa ha sido barrida y que todo está en orden.

sw.L: Naye akifika, huikuta [nyumba] imefagiwa na kupangwa vizuri.
sw.B: Hufika na kuikuta nyumba imefagiwa na kupangwa.
sw.R: Anapofika huko, hukuta nyumba imefagiwa ikawa safi, na kila kitu kimepangwa vizuri.

decisions.choice: it finds it swept: the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: it finds it empty, swept, as in some manuscripts
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts add "empty" from Matthew 12:44. Most early manuscripts lack it. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: swept and put in order: cleaned up, but with no one living there
decisions.reason: The person has been set free, but nothing has taken the spirit's place. 11:28 says what should fill the life: hearing God's word and keeping it.

decisions.choice: the house
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the house, to make clear what is found swept.

source.text: τότε πορεύεται καὶ παραλαμβάνει ἕτερα πνεύματα πονηρότερα ἑαυτοῦ ἑπτά, καὶ εἰσελθόντα κατοικεῖ ἐκεῖ, καὶ γίνεται τὰ ἔσχατα τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκείνου χείρονα τῶν πρώτων.

records.literal_gloss: Then it goes and takes other spirits more evil than itself seven, and having entered they dwell there, and becomes the last of the man that worse than the first.

en.L: Then it goes and takes along seven other spirits more evil than itself, and having gone in they settle there; and the last [state] of that {{gender:person|man}} becomes worse than the first."
en.B: Then it goes and brings seven other spirits more evil than itself, and they go in and make their home there. In the end that {{gender:person|man}} is worse off than at the start."
en.R: Then it goes and gets seven other spirits that are even more evil than it is. They all go into the person and live there. So in the end that person is worse off than before."

es.L: Entonces va y toma consigo otros siete espíritus más malvados que él, y entrando habitan allí; y el [estado] final de {{gender:esa persona|aquel hombre}} resulta peor que el primero».
es.B: Luego va y trae otros siete espíritus peores que él, y entran y se instalan allí. Al final, {{gender:esa persona|ese hombre}} queda peor que al principio».
es.R: Después va y busca otros siete espíritus todavía más malos que él. Todos entran en la persona y viven allí. Así que al final esa persona está peor que antes».

sw.L: Kisha huenda na kuwachukua pamoja naye pepo wengine saba wabaya kupita yeye, nao huingia na kuishi humo; na [hali] ya mwisho ya mtu huyo huwa mbaya zaidi kuliko ya mwanzo."
sw.B: Kisha huenda kuleta pepo wengine saba walio waovu zaidi kuliko yeye, nao huingia na kufanya makao humo. Mwishowe mtu huyo huwa katika hali mbaya kuliko alivyokuwa mwanzoni."
sw.R: Kisha huenda kuwaleta pepo wengine saba walio wabaya zaidi kuliko yeye. Wote huingia ndani ya mtu huyo na kuishi humo. Kwa hiyo mwishowe mtu huyo huwa katika hali mbaya kuliko awali."

decisions.choice: seven: a full number
decisions.reason: Seven stands for completeness. The person is now wholly in the power of evil (compare the seven demons of 8:2).

decisions.choice: worse than the first: being set free from evil is not enough
alternatives: a story about one case only
decisions.reason: The warning follows 11:23: a life emptied of evil but not given to Jesus is open to worse.

decisions.choice: the last [things]: the final condition
decisions.reason: The plural means the state the person ends up in, compared with the state at the start.

decisions.choice: person as the default, man as the alternative
decisions.reason: As in 11:24. Readable says "that person".

decisions.choice: is worse off than at the start (B); than before (R)
alternatives: the last state is worse than the first
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say it in everyday words.

source.text: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ λέγειν αὐτὸν ταῦτα ἐπάρασά τις φωνὴν γυνὴ ἐκ τοῦ ὄχλου εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Μακαρία ἡ κοιλία ἡ βαστάσασά σε καὶ μαστοὶ οὓς ἐθήλασας·

records.literal_gloss: It came about then in the saying him these things, having lifted up a certain voice a woman from the crowd said to him, Blessed the womb having borne you and breasts that you nursed.

en.L: And it happened, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was saying these things, a certain woman from the crowd, raising [her] voice, said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Blessed [is] the womb that bore {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and the breasts {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} nursed from!"
en.B: While {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was saying these things, a woman in the crowd called out to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Blessed is the woman who carried {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in her womb and fed {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} at her breasts!"
en.R: While Jesus was saying these things, a woman in the crowd shouted to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "How blessed {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} mother is! She carried {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} inside her body and fed {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} at her breast!"

es.L: Y sucedió que, mientras {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} decía estas cosas, una mujer de la multitud, alzando [la] voz, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «¡Dichoso el vientre que {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} llevó, y los pechos que mamaste!».
es.B: Mientras {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} decía estas cosas, una mujer de entre la gente {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} gritó: «¡Dichosa la mujer que {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} llevó en su vientre y {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} amamantó!».
es.R: Mientras Jesús decía estas cosas, una mujer de entre la gente {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} gritó: «¡Qué dichosa es {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} madre! Ella {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} llevó dentro de su cuerpo y {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} dio el pecho».

sw.L: Basi alipokuwa akinena mambo hayo, mwanamke fulani kutoka kwenye umati aliinua sauti yake akamwambia, "Heri tumbo lililokubeba, na matiti uliyoyanyonya!"
sw.B: Alipokuwa akisema hayo, mwanamke mmoja katika umati alimwita kwa sauti, "Heri mwanamke aliyekubeba tumboni mwake na kukunyonyesha!"
sw.R: Yesu alipokuwa akisema hayo, mwanamke mmoja katika umati alipaza sauti, akamwambia, "Mama {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} ana heri kubwa kweli! Alikubeba tumboni mwake na kukunyonyesha!"

decisions.choice: the womb and the breasts: a way of praising a son by praising his mother
decisions.reason: To call the mother blessed is to praise the son she bore. The woman honors Jesus through his mother.

decisions.choice: blessed: happy, favored by God
decisions.reason: The same word is used of Mary in 1:45, and Mary said that all generations would call her blessed (1:48).

decisions.choice: the woman who carried you in her womb (B); your mother (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the mother the woman is praising.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus where the Greek has a pronoun or leaves the subject unstated, so young readers can follow who is acting.

decisions.choice: Dichoso, dichosa
decisions.reason: As the term sheet settles for the whole New Testament: the word is happy, favored by God (meaning decision m2). "Bendito" would say that people praise someone, not that God favors them. The same in 11:28.

source.text: αὐτὸς δὲ εἶπεν· Μενοῦν μακάριοι οἱ ἀκούοντες τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ φυλάσσοντες.

records.literal_gloss: He then said, Rather blessed those hearing the word of God and keeping.

en.L: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Rather, blessed [are] those who hear the word of God and keep [it]."
en.B: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Even more blessed are those who hear the word of God and keep it."
en.R: But Jesus answered, "Yes, but the people who hear the word of God and obey it are even more blessed."

es.L: Pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} dijo: «Más bien, dichosos los que oyen la palabra de Dios y [la] guardan».
es.B: Pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} dijo: «Más dichosos aún son los que oyen la palabra de Dios y la guardan».
es.R: Pero Jesús le respondió: «Sí, pero todavía más dichosos son los que oyen la palabra de Dios y la obedecen».

sw.L: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} akasema, "Zaidi ya hayo, heri wale wanaolisikia neno la Mungu na kulishika."
sw.B: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} akasema, "Heri zaidi wale wanaolisikia neno la Mungu na kulishika."
sw.R: Lakini Yesu akajibu, "Ndiyo, lakini watu wanaolisikia neno la Mungu na kulitii wana heri zaidi."

decisions.choice: rather: yes, but even more
decisions.reason: The word can correct what was said or add to it. Luke has already shown Mary as blessed (1:42, 45, 48), so Jesus does not deny the woman's words. He points to what matters more: hearing and keeping God's word, as Mary herself did (1:38; 2:19, 51; 8:21).

decisions.choice: keep: obey and hold on to
decisions.reason: To keep God's word is to treasure it and live by it (8:15).

decisions.choice: obey it
decisions.reason: Readable says what keeping the word means.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus where the Greek has a pronoun or leaves the subject unstated, so young readers can follow who is acting.

source.text: Τῶν δὲ ὄχλων ἐπαθροιζομένων ἤρξατο λέγειν· Ἡ γενεὰ αὕτη γενεὰ πονηρά ἐστιν· σημεῖον ζητεῖ, καὶ σημεῖον οὐ δοθήσεται αὐτῇ εἰ μὴ τὸ σημεῖον Ἰωνᾶ.

records.literal_gloss: Of the now crowds pressing together he began to say, The generation this generation evil is; a sign it seeks, and a sign not will be given to it except the sign of Jonah.

en.L: And as the crowds were gathering together, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} began to say, "This generation is an evil generation; it seeks a sign, and a sign will not be given to it except the sign of Jonah.
en.B: With the crowds pressing in more and more, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} began to say, "This generation is an evil one. It looks for a sign, yet the only sign it will be given is the sign of Jonah.
en.R: More and more people were crowding around Jesus. He said, "The people living today are evil. They want {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to give them a sign. But the only sign they will get is the sign of Jonah.

es.L: Y como las multitudes se agolpaban, comenzó a decir: «Esta generación es una generación malvada; busca una señal, y no se le dará señal sino la señal de Jonás.
es.B: Mientras la multitud seguía creciendo a su alrededor, comenzó a decir: «Esta generación es malvada. Busca una señal, pero la única señal que se le dará es la señal de Jonás.
es.R: Cada vez más gente se amontonaba alrededor de Jesús. Él dijo: «La gente que vive hoy es mala. Quieren que yo les dé una señal. Pero la única señal que tendrán es la señal de Jonás.

sw.L: Na makutano walipokuwa wakizidi kukusanyika, alianza kusema, "Kizazi hiki ni kizazi kiovu; kinataka ishara, lakini ishara haitatolewa kwake ila ile ishara ya Yona.
sw.B: Makutano walipozidi kusongamana, alianza kusema, "Kizazi hiki ni kizazi kiovu. Kinatafuta ishara, lakini ishara pekee kitakayopewa ni ishara ya Yona.
sw.R: Watu wengi zaidi na zaidi walikuwa wakijazana kumzunguka Yesu. Akasema, "Watu wa siku hizi ni waovu. Wanataka {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} niwape ishara. Lakini ishara pekee watakayopata ni ishara ya Yona.

decisions.choice: generation: the people of this time
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of the people of his day as a whole, as in 7:31 and 9:41.

decisions.choice: sign: the proof from heaven they demanded
decisions.reason: This answers those who asked for a sign from heaven (11:16).

decisions.choice: the sign of Jonah: Jonah and his message to Nineveh
alternatives: a new wonder like the great fish
decisions.reason: 11:30 and 11:32 explain it: Jonah came to Nineveh with God's warning, and the city turned from its sin (Jonah 3).

decisions.choice: the crowds pressing together: the crowds growing larger
decisions.reason: The verb pictures crowds thronging together in greater numbers.

decisions.choice: The people living today
decisions.reason: Readable says who "this generation" is.

decisions.choice: They want me to give them a sign
decisions.reason: Readable names who is being asked for a sign.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus where the Greek has a pronoun or leaves the subject unstated, so young readers can follow who is acting.

source.text: καθὼς γὰρ ἐγένετο Ἰωνᾶς τοῖς Νινευίταις σημεῖον, οὕτως ἔσται καὶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου τῇ γενεᾷ ταύτῃ.

records.literal_gloss: Just as for became Jonah to the Ninevites a sign, so will be also the Son of the Man to the generation this.
