en.L: For just as Jonah became a sign to the Ninevites, so also the Son of Man will be to this generation.
en.B: For just as Jonah was a sign to the people of Nineveh, the Son of Man will be a sign to this generation.
en.R: Jonah was a sign to the people who lived in the city of Nineveh. In the same way, the Son of Man will be a sign to the people living today.

es.L: Porque así como Jonás llegó a ser señal para los ninivitas, así también lo será el Hijo del Hombre para esta generación.
es.B: Porque así como Jonás fue una señal para la gente de Nínive, el Hijo del Hombre será una señal para esta generación.
es.R: Jonás fue una señal para la gente que vivía en la ciudad de Nínive. De la misma manera, el Hijo del Hombre será una señal para la gente que vive hoy.

sw.L: Kwa maana jinsi Yona alivyokuwa ishara kwa Waninawi, ndivyo Mwana wa Adamu naye atakavyokuwa kwa kizazi hiki.
sw.B: Yona alikuwa ishara kwa watu wa Ninawi, na Mwana wa Adamu naye atakuwa ishara kwa kizazi hiki vivyo hivyo.
sw.R: Yona alikuwa ishara kwa watu walioishi katika mji wa Ninawi. Vivyo hivyo, Mwana wa Adamu atakuwa ishara kwa watu wanaoishi leo.

decisions.choice: how Jonah was a sign: he came to Nineveh as one rescued by God, with God's warning
alternatives: only his time in the great fish
decisions.reason: God brought Jonah up alive from the sea and sent him to preach to Nineveh (Jonah 2-3). Matthew 12:40 draws out the three days in the fish; Luke puts the weight on Jonah's preaching (11:32).

decisions.choice: will be: pointing to what is still to come
decisions.reason: The future may point to Jesus' rising from the dead, or to the Son of Man's coming as judge, which the next verses speak of. Either way, God will give no other sign than the Son of Man himself.

decisions.choice: Ninevites: the people of Nineveh, capital of Assyria
decisions.reason: Nineveh was the great city of Assyria, Israel's enemy (Jonah 1:2; 3:3).

decisions.choice: the Son of Man: Jesus' name for himself, recalling Daniel 7:13-14
decisions.reason: As in 5:24 and 9:22.

decisions.choice: a sign (repeated)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable repeat "a sign", which the Greek leaves understood.

decisions.choice: Mwana wa Adamu
decisions.reason: As the term sheet settles for the whole New Testament: the settled Swahili title (meaning decision m4), never under the gender setting. "Mwana wa Mtu" is more literal.

source.text: βασίλισσα νότου ἐγερθήσεται ἐν τῇ κρίσει μετὰ τῶν ἀνδρῶν τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης καὶ κατακρινεῖ αὐτούς· ὅτι ἦλθεν ἐκ τῶν περάτων τῆς γῆς ἀκοῦσαι τὴν σοφίαν Σολομῶνος, καὶ ἰδοὺ πλεῖον Σολομῶνος ὧδε.

records.literal_gloss: The queen of the South will rise up in the judgment with the men of the generation this and will condemn them; for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and behold, greater than Solomon here.

en.L: [The] queen of [the] South will rise up in the judgment with the {{gender:people|men}} of this generation and will condemn them, for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and look, [something] greater than Solomon [is] here.
en.B: At the judgment the queen of the South will stand up with the {{gender:people|men}} of this generation and condemn them, because she came from the far ends of the earth to listen to Solomon's wisdom; and here is something greater than Solomon.
en.R: On the day of judgment, the queen from the south will stand up with the {{gender:people|men}} living today and show that they are guilty. She came from a land very far away to listen to Solomon's wise teaching. And something greater than Solomon is right here!

es.L: [La] reina del sur se levantará en el juicio con {{gender:las personas|los hombres}} de esta generación y {{gender:las|los}} condenará, porque ella vino desde los confines de la tierra para oír la sabiduría de Salomón, y {{plural_you:miren|mirad}}, [algo] más que Salomón [hay] aquí.
es.B: En el juicio, la reina del sur se levantará con {{gender:las personas|los hombres}} de esta generación y {{gender:las|los}} condenará, porque ella vino desde los extremos de la tierra para escuchar la sabiduría de Salomón; y aquí hay algo mayor que Salomón.
es.R: En el día del juicio, la reina del sur se pondrá de pie junto a {{gender:las personas|los hombres}} de hoy y demostrará su culpa. Ella vino desde una tierra muy lejana para escuchar las sabias enseñanzas de Salomón. ¡Y aquí mismo hay algo más grande que Salomón!

sw.L: Malkia wa kusini atainuka katika hukumu pamoja na watu wa kizazi hiki, naye atawatia hatiani; kwa sababu alikuja kutoka miisho ya dunia kusikiliza hekima ya Sulemani, na tazama, [kitu] kikubwa kuliko Sulemani [kipo] hapa.
sw.B: Katika hukumu, malkia wa kusini atasimama pamoja na watu wa kizazi hiki na kuwatia hatiani, kwa sababu yeye alisafiri kutoka miisho ya dunia kuja kusikiliza hekima ya Sulemani; na hapa kuna kitu kikubwa kuliko Sulemani.
sw.R: Siku ya hukumu, malkia wa kusini atasimama pamoja na watu wa leo na kuonyesha kwamba wana hatia. Alikuja kutoka nchi ya mbali sana ili asikilize mafundisho ya hekima ya Sulemani. Na kitu kikubwa kuliko Sulemani kiko hapa hapa!

decisions.choice: the queen of the South: the queen of Sheba, 1 Kings 10:1-13
decisions.reason: The queen of Sheba heard of Solomon's wisdom and came from far away to test him with hard questions (1 Kings 10:1-13; 2 Chronicles 9:1-12). Sheba lay far to the south of Israel.

decisions.choice: will rise up in the judgment: will stand up at God's final judgment, as a witness
alternatives: will be raised from the dead at the judgment
decisions.reason: The words picture a court, where a witness stands up to speak. Her coming to hear Solomon will show up the people who will not listen to Jesus. The verb is also used of rising from the dead, and both may be in view.

decisions.choice: something greater: the word is neuter
decisions.reason: Jesus does not say "someone" but "something": what is happening in his words and work, God's kingdom coming. That includes Jesus himself.

decisions.choice: the men of this generation: the people of this time
decisions.reason: The word usually means men, but here it stands for the whole generation, as in 11:32. Some see a contrast: a woman from far away listened, while those here do not.

decisions.choice: people as the default, men as the alternative
decisions.reason: The whole generation is meant, men and women.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered as a separate word, or "now" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word to draw attention to what follows. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal says "look", and Balanced and Readable carry the force in the flow of the sentence, as in Matthew 1:20.

decisions.choice: show that they are guilty
decisions.reason: Readable says what condemning means here: her example proves them guilty.

decisions.choice: {{gender:las personas|los hombres}} ... {{gender:las|los}} condenará
decisions.reason: The English puts "people" and "men" under the gender setting (meaning decision m4). In Spanish the pronoun that refers back agrees with the noun, so it takes its own span (las|los); the two read together. The same in 11:32.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:miren|mirad}}
decisions.reason: The term sheet's Literal "mira" for this word; Jesus speaks to the crowd, so it is plural and takes the reader setting. Balanced and Readable leave it out, as the English does. The same in 11:32 and 11:41.

decisions.choice: watu, with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English offers "men" as the traditional alternative to "people" here and in 11:32, 11:44 and 11:46. "Watu" already means anyone, man or woman, so Swahili needs no span; "wanaume" would mean males only.

decisions.choice: kitu kikubwa, in the ki-class
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 12:41-42: the Greek word is neuter, "something" greater (meaning decision m3), so Swahili uses the ki-class "kitu kikubwa" here and in 11:32 rather than deciding that a person is meant ("aliye mkuu").

source.text: ἄνδρες Νινευῖται ἀναστήσονται ἐν τῇ κρίσει μετὰ τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης καὶ κατακρινοῦσιν αὐτήν· ὅτι μετενόησαν εἰς τὸ κήρυγμα Ἰωνᾶ, καὶ ἰδοὺ πλεῖον Ἰωνᾶ ὧδε.

records.literal_gloss: Men of Nineveh will stand up in the judgment with the generation this and will condemn it; for they repented at the preaching of Jonah, and behold, greater than Jonah here.

en.L: [The] {{gender:people|men}} of Nineveh will stand up in the judgment with this generation and will condemn it, for they repented at the preaching of Jonah, and look, [something] greater than Jonah [is] here.
en.B: At the judgment the {{gender:people|men}} of Nineveh will stand up with this generation and condemn it, because they repented when Jonah preached; and here is something greater than Jonah.
en.R: On the day of judgment, the {{gender:people|men}} of Nineveh will also stand up with the people living today and show that they are guilty. The people of Nineveh turned away from their sins when Jonah preached to them. And something greater than Jonah is right here!

es.L: {{gender:[Las] personas|[Los] hombres}} de Nínive se levantarán en el juicio con esta generación y la condenarán, porque se arrepintieron ante la predicación de Jonás, y {{plural_you:miren|mirad}}, [algo] más que Jonás [hay] aquí.
es.B: En el juicio, {{gender:las personas|los hombres}} de Nínive se levantarán con esta generación y la condenarán, porque se arrepintieron cuando Jonás predicó; y aquí hay algo mayor que Jonás.
es.R: En el día del juicio, también {{gender:las personas|los hombres}} de Nínive se pondrán de pie junto a la gente de hoy y demostrarán su culpa. La gente de Nínive se apartó de sus pecados cuando Jonás les predicó. ¡Y aquí mismo hay algo más grande que Jonás!

sw.L: Watu wa Ninawi watasimama katika hukumu pamoja na kizazi hiki na kukitia hatiani, kwa sababu walitubu waliposikia mahubiri ya Yona; na tazama, [kitu] kikubwa kuliko Yona [kipo] hapa.
sw.B: Katika hukumu watu wa Ninawi watasimama pamoja na kizazi hiki na kukitia hatiani, kwa sababu walitubu Yona alipohubiri; na hapa kuna kitu kikubwa kuliko Yona.
sw.R: Siku ya hukumu, watu wa Ninawi nao watasimama pamoja na watu wa leo na kuonyesha kwamba wana hatia. Watu wa Ninawi waliacha dhambi zao Yona alipowahubiria. Na kitu kikubwa kuliko Yona kiko hapa hapa!

decisions.choice: they repented at the preaching of Jonah: Jonah 3:5-10
decisions.reason: When Jonah preached, the people of Nineveh believed God, fasted and turned from their evil ways, and God spared the city.

decisions.choice: repented: turned from their wrong ways to God
decisions.reason: Repentance is a change of heart and life (3:3, 8).

decisions.choice: will stand up in the judgment: will rise as witnesses at God's judgment
decisions.reason: As in 11:31.

decisions.choice: something greater: the word is neuter
decisions.reason: As in 11:31.

decisions.choice: people as the default, men as the alternative
decisions.reason: The whole city repented, men and women (Jonah 3:5).

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered as a separate word, or "now" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word to draw attention to what follows. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal says "look", and Balanced and Readable carry the force in the flow of the sentence, as in Matthew 1:20.

decisions.choice: turned away from their sins (R); repented (L, B)
decisions.reason: Readable says what repenting means.

source.text: Οὐδεὶς λύχνον ἅψας εἰς κρύπτην τίθησιν οὐδὲ ὑπὸ τὸν μόδιον ἀλλ’ ἐπὶ τὴν λυχνίαν, ἵνα οἱ εἰσπορευόμενοι τὸ φέγγος βλέπωσιν.

records.literal_gloss: No one a lamp having lit into a hidden place puts nor under the basket but on the lampstand, that those entering the light may see.

en.L: No one, having lit a lamp, puts [it] in a hidden place or under the basket, but on the lampstand, so that those who come in may see the light.
en.B: A lamp, once lit, is not hidden away in a cellar or put under a basket; it is set on a lampstand, where anyone coming in will see its light.
en.R: When someone lights a lamp, it is not hidden or put under a basket. It is put on a lampstand, so that people who come into the house can see by its light.

es.L: Nadie, después de encender una lámpara, [la] pone en un lugar escondido ni debajo del cesto, sino sobre el candelero, para que los que entran vean la luz.
es.B: Una lámpara encendida no se esconde en un sótano ni se pone debajo de un cesto; se coloca sobre el candelero, para que todo el que entre vea su luz.
es.R: Cuando alguien enciende una lámpara, no la esconde ni la pone debajo de un cesto. La pone sobre un candelero, para que los que entran en la casa puedan ver con su luz.

sw.L: Hakuna mtu ambaye, baada ya kuwasha taa, huiweka mahali palipofichika wala chini ya pishi, bali juu ya kinara, ili wanaoingia waione nuru.
sw.B: Taa iliyowashwa haifichwi katika chumba cha chini wala haiwekwi chini ya pishi; huwekwa juu ya kinara, ili kila anayeingia aione nuru yake.
sw.R: Mtu akiwasha taa, haifichi wala haiweki chini ya kikapu. Huiweka juu ya kinara, ili watu wanaoingia nyumbani waweze kuona kwa nuru yake.

decisions.choice: or under the basket: included, as in the SBLGNT
alternatives: the words left out, as in some early manuscripts
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts, including the papyri P45 and P75, lack "or under the basket". The words may have come in from Matthew 5:15 and Mark 4:21, or been lost by accident. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: a hidden place: a cellar or a hidden corner
decisions.reason: The word can mean a cellar or vault, a place out of sight.

decisions.choice: the basket: a container used to measure grain
decisions.reason: The word names a measure for grain, holding about two gallons, and the container used for it.

decisions.choice: the lamp: God's light, plainly shown
alternatives: a saying unrelated to what comes before
decisions.reason: Jesus used the picture in 8:16. Here it follows the demand for a sign: God has not hidden his light. The question is whether people see it (11:34-36).

decisions.choice: the lamp as subject, in the passive
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the lamp the subject, which reads easily and avoids a vague "they".

decisions.choice: cesto
decisions.reason: The word is a container used to measure grain (meaning decision m3). "Almud" names the measure but few readers know it, and "cajón" (a drawer or box) is another object; "cesto" gives the picture, as the English "basket" does.

decisions.choice: pishi (L, B); kikapu (R)
decisions.reason: The word is a container used to measure grain (meaning decision m3), which is what "pishi" is; Readable says "kikapu" (basket), as the English does.

source.text: ὁ λύχνος τοῦ σώματός ἐστιν ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου.

records.literal_gloss: The lamp of the body is the eye of you.

en.L: The lamp of the body is your eye.
en.B: Your body's lamp is your eye.
en.R: Your eye is like a lamp for your body.

es.L: La lámpara del cuerpo es tu ojo.
es.B: La lámpara de tu cuerpo es tu ojo.
es.R: Tu ojo es como una lámpara para tu cuerpo.

sw.L: Taa ya mwili ni jicho lako.
sw.B: Jicho lako ndilo taa ya mwili wako.
sw.R: Jicho lako ni kama taa kwa mwili wako.

decisions.choice: the lamp of the body: the eye lets light into the whole body
decisions.reason: The eye is pictured as the opening through which light reaches the whole person.

decisions.choice: like a lamp
decisions.reason: Readable makes the comparison plain.

source.text: ὅταν ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου ἁπλοῦς ᾖ, καὶ ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου φωτεινόν ἐστιν· ἐπὰν δὲ πονηρὸς ᾖ, καὶ τὸ σῶμά σου σκοτεινόν.

records.literal_gloss: When the eye of you clear is, also all the body of you full of light is; when however evil it is, also the body of you dark.

en.L: When your eye is sound, your whole body also is full of light; but when it is evil, your body also [is] dark.
en.B: If your eye is clear, light fills your whole body as well. If your eye is bad, darkness fills your body too.
en.R: If your eye is healthy, light fills your whole body. But if your eye is bad, your body is in darkness.

es.L: Cuando tu ojo es sano, también todo tu cuerpo está lleno de luz; pero cuando es malo, también tu cuerpo [está] a oscuras.
es.B: Si tu ojo está limpio, la luz llena también todo tu cuerpo. Si tu ojo está malo, la oscuridad llena también tu cuerpo.
es.R: Si tu ojo está sano, la luz llena todo tu cuerpo. Pero si tu ojo está malo, tu cuerpo queda en oscuridad.

sw.L: Jicho lako likiwa zima, mwili wako wote pia umejaa nuru; lakini likiwa ovu, mwili wako nao [umo] gizani.
sw.B: Jicho lako likiwa safi, nuru hujaza mwili wako wote pia. Jicho lako likiwa baya, giza hujaza mwili wako pia.
sw.R: Jicho lako likiwa na afya, nuru hujaza mwili wako wote. Lakini jicho lako likiwa baya, mwili wako huwa gizani.

decisions.choice: sound: healthy and clear; also single-minded and generous
decisions.reason: The word means simple, single, without a fold. Used of an eye, it means healthy. It is also used of a sincere, generous heart (Romans 12:8, "generously"). Both senses may be heard here.

decisions.choice: evil: diseased; also the "evil eye" of a grudging heart
decisions.reason: A bad eye cannot see. In Scripture an evil eye is also a picture of a mean or envious heart (Deuteronomy 15:9; Proverbs 28:22).

decisions.choice: the eye: the way a person takes in God's light
decisions.reason: The saying follows the demand for a sign. The light is there (11:33); the trouble is an eye that will not take it in.

decisions.choice: sound ... evil (L); clear ... bad (B); healthy ... bad (R)
decisions.reason: Each level uses words that suit an eye; the decisions above give the other senses.

decisions.choice: malo
decisions.reason: The word is "evil": an eye that is diseased, and also the "evil eye" of a grudging heart (meaning decision m2). Spanish "malo" keeps both, since "estar malo" is also to be sick; "enfermo" would keep only the first.

decisions.choice: ovu (L); baya (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word is "evil": an eye that is diseased, and also the "evil eye" of a grudging heart (meaning decision m2). "Jicho baya" keeps both in Swahili, where it is also the envious eye; Literal keeps the moral word "ovu".

source.text: σκόπει οὖν μὴ τὸ φῶς τὸ ἐν σοὶ σκότος ἐστίν.

records.literal_gloss: Watch therefore lest the light that in you darkness is.

en.L: Watch out, then, lest the light that [is] in you is darkness.
en.B: So be careful that the light inside you is not really darkness.
en.R: So be careful. Do not let the light inside you turn out to be darkness.

es.L: Fíjate, pues, no sea que la luz que [hay] en ti sea oscuridad.
es.B: Así que ten cuidado de que la luz que hay dentro de ti no sea en realidad oscuridad.
es.R: Así que ten cuidado. No dejes que la luz que hay dentro de ti resulte ser oscuridad.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo jihadhari, isije nuru iliyo ndani yako ikawa giza.
sw.B: Basi uwe mwangalifu, nuru iliyo ndani yako isiwe kwa kweli ni giza.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo kuwa mwangalifu. Nuru iliyo ndani yako isije ikawa ni giza.

decisions.choice: lest: a warning that it may already be so
decisions.reason: The form can express a fear that something is in fact the case: check whether what you take for light is really darkness.

decisions.choice: really (B); turn out to be (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out the sense of the warning.

source.text: εἰ οὖν τὸ σῶμά σου ὅλον φωτεινόν, μὴ ἔχον μέρος τι σκοτεινόν, ἔσται φωτεινὸν ὅλον ὡς ὅταν ὁ λύχνος τῇ ἀστραπῇ φωτίζῃ σε.

records.literal_gloss: If therefore the body of you full of light, not having part any dark, will be full of light wholly as when the lamp with the brightness may light you.

en.L: If then your whole body [is] full of light, not having any part dark, it will be wholly full of light, as when the lamp lights you with [its] brightness."
en.B: So if light fills your whole body and no part of it is dark, it will be bright all through, as when a lamp shines on you with its beam."
en.R: If your whole body is full of light, with no dark part at all, then you will be full of light. It will be like having a bright lamp shining on you."

es.L: Si, pues, todo tu cuerpo [está] lleno de luz, sin tener parte alguna a oscuras, estará todo lleno de luz, como cuando la lámpara te alumbra con [su] resplandor».
es.B: Así que, si la luz llena todo tu cuerpo y ninguna parte de él está a oscuras, estará completamente iluminado, como cuando una lámpara te alumbra con su resplandor».
es.R: Si todo tu cuerpo está lleno de luz, sin ninguna parte oscura, entonces estarás lleno de luz. Será como tener una lámpara brillante que te alumbra».

sw.L: Basi ikiwa mwili wako wote [umejaa] nuru, bila kuwa na sehemu yoyote yenye giza, utajaa nuru kabisa, kama wakati taa inapokuangazia kwa mng'ao [wake]."
sw.B: Basi nuru ikijaza mwili wako wote, na hakuna sehemu yake yenye giza, utang'aa wote kabisa, kama taa inapokumulikia kwa mng'ao wake."
sw.R: Mwili wako wote ukijaa nuru, bila sehemu yoyote yenye giza, basi utajaa nuru. Itakuwa kama kuwa na taa angavu inayokuangazia."

decisions.choice: it will be wholly full of light: the result of having no dark part
alternatives: a simple repetition of the first half
decisions.reason: The second half seems to repeat the first. The weight falls on "wholly" and on the comparison: a life with no part kept back from God's light will shine all through, like someone in a lamp's full light. Some take the future to point to the last day.

decisions.choice: brightness: a flash or gleam of light
decisions.reason: The word is used of lightning (10:18; 17:24), and here of a lamp's bright light.

decisions.choice: two sentences
decisions.reason: Readable gives the comparison its own sentence.

source.text: Ἐν δὲ τῷ λαλῆσαι ἐρωτᾷ αὐτὸν Φαρισαῖος ὅπως ἀριστήσῃ παρ’ αὐτῷ· εἰσελθὼν δὲ ἀνέπεσεν.

records.literal_gloss: In then the speaking, asks him a Pharisee that he would dine with him; having entered then he reclined.

en.L: Now as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke, a Pharisee asks {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to dine with him; and having gone in, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} reclined [at table].
en.B: As {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} finished speaking, a Pharisee asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to eat at his home, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went in and took {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} place at the table.
en.R: When Jesus finished talking, a Pharisee asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to come and eat at his house. So Jesus went in and took {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} place at the table.

es.L: Mientras hablaba, un fariseo {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} pide que coma con él; y, habiendo entrado, se recostó [a la mesa].
es.B: Cuando terminó de hablar, un fariseo {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} invitó a comer en su casa, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} entró y ocupó {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} lugar a la mesa.
es.R: Cuando Jesús terminó de hablar, un fariseo {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} invitó a comer en su casa. Así que Jesús entró y ocupó {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} lugar a la mesa.

sw.L: Basi alipokuwa akisema, Farisayo mmoja anamwomba ale chakula kwake; naye akaingia, akaegama [mezani].
sw.B: Alipomaliza kusema, Farisayo mmoja alimkaribisha ale chakula nyumbani kwake, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} akaingia, akakaa mahali {{deity_pronoun:pake|Pake}} mezani.
sw.R: Yesu alipomaliza kuongea, Farisayo mmoja alimkaribisha aje kula nyumbani kwake. Basi Yesu akaingia, akakaa mahali {{deity_pronoun:pake|Pake}} mezani.

decisions.choice: Pharisee: one of a movement of Jews devoted to keeping God's law in every part of life
decisions.reason: As explained at 5:17 and 6:2. Pharisees kept the law strictly, together with the traditions about how to keep it, including rules about washing (Mark 7:3-4).

decisions.choice: as he spoke: as he finished, or just after
decisions.reason: The form can mean while he was speaking or when he had spoken. The invitation comes straight after the sayings of 11:29-36.

decisions.choice: dine: the word for an early or midday meal
decisions.reason: The word usually means the first meal of the day, eaten in the morning or around noon (compare 14:12).

decisions.choice: reclined: lay on a couch at the table, as guests did at a meal
decisions.reason: At a formal meal guests lay on couches around a low table, leaning on the left elbow (7:36-38).

decisions.choice: took his place at the table
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable describe the meal in words a modern reader knows; the decision on "reclined" explains the custom.

decisions.choice: asked (past tense)
decisions.reason: The Greek uses the present tense to tell the story vividly. Literal keeps it; Balanced and Readable use the past.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus where the Greek has a pronoun or leaves the subject unstated, so young readers can follow who is acting.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Φαρισαῖος ἰδὼν ἐθαύμασεν ὅτι οὐ πρῶτον ἐβαπτίσθη πρὸ τοῦ ἀρίστου.

records.literal_gloss: And the Pharisee having seen marveled that not first he washed before the dinner.

en.L: And the Pharisee, seeing [it], was amazed that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not first wash before the meal.
en.B: The Pharisee saw that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had not washed before the meal, and it surprised him.
en.R: The Pharisee was surprised to see that Jesus did not first wash {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} before the meal, as their custom required.

es.L: Y el fariseo, al ver[lo], se asombró de que no se lavara primero antes de la comida.
es.B: El fariseo vio que no se había lavado antes de la comida, y se sorprendió.
es.R: El fariseo se sorprendió al ver que Jesús no se lavó primero antes de comer, como lo exigía su costumbre.

sw.L: Na yule Farisayo, alipoona, alishangaa kwamba hakujiosha kwanza kabla ya mlo.
sw.B: Farisayo huyo aliona kwamba hakujiosha kabla ya mlo, akashangaa.
sw.R: Farisayo huyo alishangaa kuona kwamba Yesu hakujiosha kwanza kabla ya kula, kama desturi yao ilivyotaka.

decisions.choice: wash: a washing for religious purity before eating
decisions.reason: The verb is the word for baptizing, to dip or wash. Many Jews, the Pharisees especially, washed before eating to be clean before God, by a tradition handed down from the elders (Mark 7:3-4). The law of Moses did not require it of ordinary people.

decisions.choice: having seen: he noticed and wondered
decisions.reason: Luke does not say the Pharisee said anything; Jesus answers what he saw in him.

decisions.choice: as their custom required
decisions.reason: Readable says why the Pharisee expected Jesus to wash.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus where the Greek has a pronoun or leaves the subject unstated, so young readers can follow who is acting.

source.text: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ κύριος πρὸς αὐτόν· Νῦν ὑμεῖς οἱ Φαρισαῖοι τὸ ἔξωθεν τοῦ ποτηρίου καὶ τοῦ πίνακος καθαρίζετε, τὸ δὲ ἔσωθεν ὑμῶν γέμει ἁρπαγῆς καὶ πονηρίας.

records.literal_gloss: Said then the Lord to him, Now you the Pharisees the outside of the cup and of the dish you cleanse, the and inside of you is full of plunder and wickedness.

en.L: But the Lord said to him, "Now you Pharisees cleanse the outside of the cup and the dish, but your inside is full of plunder and wickedness.
en.B: But the Lord said to him, "You Pharisees clean the cup and the dish on the outside, but your own insides are full of plunder and wickedness.
en.R: Then the Lord said to him, "You Pharisees wash the outside of your cups and dishes. But inside, you are full of greed for what belongs to others, and full of evil.

es.L: Pero el Señor le dijo: «Ahora {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, los fariseos, {{plural_you:limpian|limpiáis}} lo de fuera de la copa y del plato, pero {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} interior está lleno de rapiña y maldad.
es.B: Pero el Señor le dijo: «{{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}}, los fariseos, {{plural_you:limpian|limpiáis}} la copa y el plato por fuera, pero {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} propio interior está lleno de robo y de maldad.
es.R: Entonces el Señor le dijo: «{{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}}, los fariseos, {{plural_you:lavan|laváis}} {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} copas y {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} platos por fuera. Pero por dentro {{plural_you:están|estáis}} llenos de codicia por lo que es de otros, y llenos de maldad.

sw.L: Lakini Bwana akamwambia, "Sasa ninyi Mafarisayo, mnaisafisha sehemu ya nje ya kikombe na ya sahani, lakini sehemu yenu ya ndani imejaa uporaji na uovu.
sw.B: Lakini Bwana akamwambia, "Ninyi Mafarisayo mnasafisha kikombe na sahani kwa nje, lakini nafsi zenu za ndani zimejaa uporaji na uovu.
sw.R: Kisha Bwana akamwambia, "Ninyi Mafarisayo mnaosha vikombe na sahani zenu kwa nje. Lakini mioyoni mwenu mmejaa tamaa ya kuchukua vitu vya wengine, na mmejaa uovu.

decisions.choice: the Lord: Luke's name for Jesus in the story
decisions.reason: Luke the narrator often calls Jesus "the Lord" (7:13, 19; 10:1).

decisions.choice: cleanse the outside of the cup: rules for keeping vessels ritually clean
decisions.reason: The law gave rules for vessels that had become unclean (Leviticus 11:32-33), and tradition added more (Mark 7:4). Jesus uses the practice as a picture.

decisions.choice: plunder: robbery, grasping greed
decisions.reason: The word means taking things by force, and the greed behind it.

decisions.choice: your inside: you yourselves, within
decisions.reason: The picture turns from the cup to the people: their hearts are full of greed.

decisions.choice: greed for what belongs to others, and full of evil
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word for plunder.

source.text: ἄφρονες, οὐχ ὁ ποιήσας τὸ ἔξωθεν καὶ τὸ ἔσωθεν ἐποίησεν;

records.literal_gloss: Fools, not the one having made the outside also the inside made?

en.L: Fools, did not the one who made the outside also make the inside?
en.B: Foolish people! The one who made the outside made the inside as well, did {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} not?
en.R: You foolish people! God made the outside, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made the inside too.

es.L: Insensatos, ¿no hizo también lo de dentro el que hizo lo de fuera?
es.B: ¡Insensatos! El que hizo lo de fuera hizo también lo de dentro, ¿no es así?
es.R: ¡Qué insensatos {{plural_you:son|sois}}! Dios hizo lo de fuera, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} hizo también lo de dentro.

sw.L: Ninyi msio na akili! Je, yule aliyefanya sehemu ya nje hakufanya pia sehemu ya ndani?
sw.B: Ninyi msio na akili! Yule aliyeumba nje aliumba na ndani pia, sivyo?
sw.R: Ninyi watu msio na akili! Mungu ndiye aliyeumba sehemu ya nje, na {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ndiye aliyeumba sehemu ya ndani pia.

decisions.choice: the one who made: God, the maker of all
alternatives: the person who makes the cup
decisions.reason: Most likely Jesus means God, who made both the outside and the inside of a person and cares about both. Some take it of the potter who makes both sides of a cup; the point is the same.

decisions.choice: fools: people without sense
decisions.reason: In Scripture a fool is someone who does not reckon with God (12:20; Psalm 14:1).

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the maker.

decisions.choice: a statement with a question at the end (B); a statement (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek question expects the answer "yes". Balanced and Readable state it.

source.text: πλὴν τὰ ἐνόντα δότε ἐλεημοσύνην, καὶ ἰδοὺ πάντα καθαρὰ ὑμῖν ἐστιν.

records.literal_gloss: But the things being within give alms, and behold, all things clean to you are.

en.L: But give as alms the things inside, and look, all things are clean for you.
en.B: Rather, give what is inside as gifts to the poor, and then everything is clean for you.
en.R: Instead, give what is inside your cups and dishes to poor people. Then everything will be clean for you.

es.L: Más bien, {{plural_you:den|dad}} como limosna lo que está dentro, y {{plural_you:miren|mirad}}, todo {{plural_you:les|os}} es limpio.
es.B: Más bien, {{plural_you:den|dad}} lo de dentro como ayuda a los pobres, y entonces todo queda limpio para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.R: En lugar de eso, {{plural_you:den|dad}} a los pobres lo que hay dentro de {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} copas y {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} platos. Entonces todo será limpio para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

sw.L: Bali vilivyomo ndani vitoeni kuwa sadaka kwa maskini, na tazama, kila kitu ni safi kwenu.
sw.B: Badala yake, wapeni maskini kile kilichomo ndani, na hapo kila kitu kitakuwa safi kwenu.
sw.R: Badala yake, wapeni maskini vitu vilivyomo ndani ya vikombe na sahani zenu. Ndipo kila kitu kitakuwa safi kwenu.

decisions.choice: the things inside: what is in the cups and dishes
alternatives: as for what is inside you, give to the poor
decisions.reason: The words can mean the contents of the cups and dishes: give that food and wealth away. They can also mean "as for what is inside", turning to the heart. Either way, generosity cleanses where washing cannot.

decisions.choice: give alms: give gifts to the poor
decisions.reason: Giving to the poor was a duty of Jewish piety (12:33; Acts 10:2).

decisions.choice: all things are clean for you: generosity, not washing, makes clean
decisions.reason: Jesus answers the Pharisee's surprise at his not washing (11:38). A heart that gives is clean, and so is what it touches.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered as a separate word, or "now" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word to draw attention to what follows. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal says "look", and Balanced and Readable carry the force in the flow of the sentence, as in Matthew 1:20.

decisions.choice: inside your cups and dishes
decisions.reason: Readable follows the reading in the first decision.

source.text: Ἀλλὰ οὐαὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς Φαρισαίοις, ὅτι ἀποδεκατοῦτε τὸ ἡδύοσμον καὶ τὸ πήγανον καὶ πᾶν λάχανον, καὶ παρέρχεσθε τὴν κρίσιν καὶ τὴν ἀγάπην τοῦ θεοῦ· ταῦτα δὲ ἔδει ποιῆσαι κἀκεῖνα μὴ παρεῖναι.

records.literal_gloss: But woe to you the Pharisees, for you tithe the mint and the rue and every herb, and pass by the justice and the love of God; these things but it was necessary to do and those not to neglect.

en.L: But woe to you Pharisees, for you tithe mint and rue and every herb, and pass over justice and the love of God; but these you ought to have done, and not neglected those.
en.B: But how terrible for you Pharisees! You set aside for God a tenth even of mint and rue and every kind of garden plant, yet you pass over justice and the love of God. Justice and love are what you should have practiced, while not neglecting the tenth.
en.R: How terrible for you Pharisees! You give one tenth of everything to God, even of the little plants you grow for flavor, like mint and rue. But you do not care about justice or about loving God. You should do these things, and keep giving a tenth as well.

es.L: Pero ¡ay de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, fariseos! Porque {{plural_you:dan|dais}} el diezmo de la menta y de la ruda y de toda hierba de huerto, y {{plural_you:pasan|pasáis}} de largo ante la justicia y el amor de Dios; pero esto {{plural_you:debían|debíais}} hacer, sin descuidar aquello.
es.B: Pero ¡ay de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, fariseos! Le {{plural_you:dan|dais}} a Dios la décima parte hasta de la menta, de la ruda y de toda clase de hierbas del huerto, pero {{plural_you:pasan|pasáis}} de largo ante la justicia y el amor a Dios. La justicia y el amor es lo que {{plural_you:debían|debíais}} practicar, sin dejar de dar la décima parte.
es.R: ¡Qué terrible será para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, fariseos! Le {{plural_you:dan|dais}} a Dios la décima parte de todo, hasta de las plantitas que {{plural_you:cultivan|cultiváis}} para dar sabor, como la menta y la ruda. Pero no {{plural_you:les|os}} importa la justicia ni amar a Dios. {{plural_you:Deberían|Deberíais}} hacer estas cosas, y seguir dando también la décima parte.

sw.L: Lakini ole wenu ninyi Mafarisayo, kwa kuwa mnatoa fungu la kumi la mnanaa na sadabu na kila mboga, na mnaipita haki na upendo wa Mungu; lakini haya ilipasa kuyafanya, bila kuyaacha yale.
sw.B: Lakini ole wenu Mafarisayo! Mnamtolea Mungu sehemu ya kumi hata ya mnanaa, sadabu na kila aina ya mboga za bustani, lakini mnaipuuza haki na upendo kwa Mungu. Haki na upendo ndivyo mlivyopaswa kutenda, bila kuacha kutoa sehemu ya kumi.
sw.R: Itakuwa vibaya mno kwenu, Mafarisayo! Mnampa Mungu sehemu moja ya kumi ya kila kitu, hata ya mimea midogo mnayoikuza ili kuongeza ladha, kama mnanaa na sadabu. Lakini hamjali haki wala kumpenda Mungu. Mnapaswa kufanya mambo hayo, na kuendelea pia kutoa sehemu ya kumi.

decisions.choice: woe: a cry of grief and warning over people facing God's judgment
decisions.reason: The prophets used the cry over those who would not turn back (Isaiah 5:8-22; Habakkuk 2:6-19). It is a lament and a warning, not a wish for harm. Jesus used it in 6:24-26.

decisions.choice: tithe: give a tenth to God
decisions.reason: The law required a tenth of grain, wine, oil and produce to be given to God (Leviticus 27:30; Deuteronomy 14:22-23). The Pharisees counted even the smallest garden herbs.

decisions.choice: mint and rue: small garden herbs
decisions.reason: Mint and rue were used for flavor and medicine. Later Jewish teaching counted rue among the plants that did not need to be tithed (Mishnah, Shebiith 9:1), so tithing it went beyond what was required.

decisions.choice: justice: doing right by others
decisions.reason: The word can mean judgment, but here it means fairness and right dealing, as the prophets demanded (Micah 6:8).

decisions.choice: the love of God: love for God
decisions.reason: Most likely the love people owe to God (Deuteronomy 6:5; Luke 10:27). Jesus sets it beside justice: love for God and right dealing with others.

decisions.choice: the last sentence included, as in the SBLGNT
alternatives: the sentence missing, as in one ancient manuscript
decisions.reason: One ancient manuscript, Codex Bezae, lacks the closing words "these you ought to have done". Nearly all others have them. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Woe to you (L); How terrible for you (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Woe" is rarely heard in everyday speech. Literal keeps the old cry; Balanced and Readable say what it means, as in the woes of 6:24-26.

decisions.choice: Justice and love ... the tenth (B); these things ... giving a tenth (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "these" and "those" refer to.

decisions.choice: the little plants you grow for flavor
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of plants these are.

decisions.choice: ¡ay de ustedes! (L, B); ¡Qué terrible será para ustedes! (R)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet settles for the whole New Testament and as in Matthew 23: "¡Ay de ustedes!" is the Spanish cry of grief and warning (meaning decision m1), kept at Balanced too, where the English says "How terrible for you"; Readable says what it means. The same in every woe of this chapter.

decisions.choice: ole wenu (L, B); Itakuwa vibaya mno kwenu (R)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet settles for the whole New Testament and as in Matthew 23: "ole wenu" is the Swahili cry of grief and warning (meaning decision m1), kept at Balanced too, where the English says "How terrible for you"; Readable says what it means. The same in every woe of this chapter.

decisions.choice: sadabu
decisions.reason: Rue is a small bitter garden herb (meaning decision m3). "Sadabu" is the name taken from Arabic, and it may not be known to many readers; a native reviewer should say whether a better-known name, or a description such as "mmea wa kukoleza", serves better. "Mchicha" (amaranth) is a different plant.

source.text: οὐαὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς Φαρισαίοις, ὅτι ἀγαπᾶτε τὴν πρωτοκαθεδρίαν ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς καὶ τοὺς ἀσπασμοὺς ἐν ταῖς ἀγοραῖς.

records.literal_gloss: Woe to you the Pharisees, for you love the first seat in the synagogues and the greetings in the marketplaces.

en.L: Woe to you Pharisees, for you love the front seat in the synagogues and the greetings in the marketplaces.
en.B: How terrible for you Pharisees! You love to sit in the front seats of the synagogues and to be greeted in the marketplaces.
en.R: How terrible for you Pharisees! You love to sit in the seats of honor in the synagogues. And you love it when people greet you with respect in the markets.

es.L: ¡Ay de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, fariseos! Porque {{plural_you:aman|amáis}} el primer asiento en las sinagogas y los saludos en las plazas.
es.B: ¡Ay de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, fariseos! {{plural_you:Les|Os}} encanta sentarse en los primeros asientos de las sinagogas y que {{plural_you:los|os}} saluden en las plazas.
es.R: ¡Qué terrible será para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, fariseos! {{plural_you:Les|Os}} encanta sentarse en los asientos de honor en las sinagogas. Y {{plural_you:les|os}} encanta que la gente {{plural_you:los|os}} salude con respeto en los mercados.

sw.L: Ole wenu Mafarisayo, kwa sababu mnapenda kiti cha mbele katika masinagogi na salamu katika masoko.
sw.B: Ole wenu Mafarisayo! Mnapenda kuketi viti vya mbele katika masinagogi na kupewa salamu za heshima sokoni.
sw.R: Itakuwa vibaya mno kwenu, Mafarisayo! Mnapenda kukaa kwenye viti vya heshima katika masinagogi. Tena mnapenda watu wawasalimu kwa heshima masokoni.

decisions.choice: the front seat: the seats of honor at the front of the synagogue
decisions.reason: The places of honor were at the front, in view of the people (20:46).

decisions.choice: greetings: public greetings of respect, with titles of honor
decisions.reason: In the busy marketplaces, respected teachers were greeted with honor (20:46).

decisions.choice: Woe to you (L); How terrible for you (B, R)
decisions.reason: The same wording for every woe in 11:42-52 (see 11:42), as in 6:24-26.

source.text: οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, ὅτι ἐστὲ ὡς τὰ μνημεῖα τὰ ἄδηλα, καὶ οἱ ἄνθρωποι οἱ περιπατοῦντες ἐπάνω οὐκ οἴδασιν.

records.literal_gloss: Woe to you, for you are like the graves the unmarked, and the men walking over not know.

en.L: Woe to you, for you are like unmarked graves, and the {{gender:people|men}} who walk over [them] do not know [it]."
en.B: How terrible for you! You are like graves with no marker, and the {{gender:people|men}} who walk over them are unaware of it."
en.R: How terrible for you! You are like graves that have no marker. People walk over them without knowing that they are there, and so they become unclean."

es.L: ¡Ay de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}! Porque {{plural_you:son|sois}} como los sepulcros que no se ven, y {{gender:las personas|los hombres}} que caminan por encima no [lo] saben».
es.B: ¡Ay de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}! {{plural_you:Son|Sois}} como sepulcros sin ninguna señal, y {{gender:las personas|los hombres}} que caminan sobre ellos no se dan cuenta».
es.R: ¡Qué terrible será para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}! {{plural_you:Son|Sois}} como tumbas que no tienen ninguna señal. La gente camina sobre ellas sin saber que están allí, y así queda impura».

sw.L: Ole wenu, kwa sababu mko kama makaburi yasiyoonekana, na watu wanaotembea juu yake hawajui."
sw.B: Ole wenu! Mko kama makaburi yasiyo na alama, na watu wanaopita juu yake hawatambui."
sw.R: Itakuwa vibaya mno kwenu! Mko kama makaburi yasiyo na alama. Watu hutembea juu yake bila kujua kwamba yapo, na hivyo wanakuwa najisi."

decisions.choice: unmarked graves: touching a grave made a person unclean
decisions.reason: Anyone who touched a grave was unclean for seven days (Numbers 19:16). Graves were marked so that people could keep away from them. Walking over an unmarked grave made a person unclean without knowing it.

decisions.choice: the point: people are made unclean by the Pharisees without knowing it
alternatives: the Pharisees are dead inside only
decisions.reason: The Pharisees, so careful about cleanness, spread uncleanness to those who follow them.

decisions.choice: Woe to you: the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: "Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites", as in many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites", the wording of Matthew 23:27. The earliest manuscripts lack it. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Woe to you (L); How terrible for you (B, R)
decisions.reason: The same wording for every woe in 11:42-52 (see 11:42), as in 6:24-26.

decisions.choice: and so they become unclean
decisions.reason: Readable says why walking over a grave mattered, from the first decision.

source.text: Ἀποκριθεὶς δέ τις τῶν νομικῶν λέγει αὐτῷ· Διδάσκαλε, ταῦτα λέγων καὶ ἡμᾶς ὑβρίζεις.

records.literal_gloss: Answering now one of the lawyers says to him, Teacher, these things saying also us you insult.

en.L: And answering, one of the experts in the law says to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Teacher, by saying these things {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} insult us also."
en.B: One of the experts in the law responded to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Teacher, by saying this {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are insulting us as well."
en.R: One of the experts in God's law said to Jesus, "Teacher, what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are saying insults us too!"

es.L: Y respondiendo, uno de los expertos en la ley {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dice: «Maestro, diciendo estas cosas también a nosotros nos insultas».
es.B: Uno de los expertos en la ley {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} respondió: «Maestro, al decir esto también nos estás insultando a nosotros».
es.R: Uno de los expertos en la ley de Dios le dijo a Jesús: «Maestro, ¡lo que dices también nos insulta a nosotros!».

sw.L: Na mmoja wa wataalamu wa sheria akijibu anamwambia, "Mwalimu, kwa kusema mambo haya unatutukana sisi pia."
sw.B: Mmoja wa wataalamu wa sheria akamjibu, "Mwalimu, kwa kusema hivi unatutukana sisi pia."
sw.R: Mmoja wa wataalamu wa sheria ya Mungu akamwambia Yesu, "Mwalimu, maneno yako yanatutukana sisi pia!"

decisions.choice: experts in the law: men trained in the law of Moses
decisions.reason: As in 7:30 and 10:25. They taught and applied God's law. Many were Pharisees, so Jesus' words about the Pharisees struck them too.

decisions.choice: insult: treat with contempt, put to shame
decisions.reason: The word means to mistreat or shame someone.

decisions.choice: experts in God's law (R); experts in the law (L, B)
decisions.reason: Today "lawyer" suggests courts and contracts. The word means someone expert in the law of Moses.

decisions.choice: says (L); responded, said (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek tells the story in the present tense. Literal keeps it.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus where the Greek has a pronoun or leaves the subject unstated, so young readers can follow who is acting.

decisions.choice: los expertos en la ley
decisions.reason: As the term sheet settles for the whole New Testament: these men were trained in the law of Moses (meaning decision m1); the name keeps them apart from the scribes of 11:53.

decisions.choice: wataalamu wa sheria
decisions.reason: As the term sheet settles for the whole New Testament: these men were trained in the law of Moses (meaning decision m1); the name keeps them apart from the scribes ("waandishi") of 11:53.

source.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Καὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς νομικοῖς οὐαί, ὅτι φορτίζετε τοὺς ἀνθρώπους φορτία δυσβάστακτα, καὶ αὐτοὶ ἑνὶ τῶν δακτύλων ὑμῶν οὐ προσψαύετε τοῖς φορτίοις.

records.literal_gloss: And he said, Also to you the lawyers woe, for you burden the men burdens heavy to bear, and yourselves with one of the fingers of you not do touch the burdens.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Woe to you experts in the law also, for you load {{gender:people|men}} with burdens hard to carry, and you yourselves do not touch the burdens with one of your fingers.
en.B: He said, "How terrible for you experts in the law too! You pile on {{gender:people|men}} loads that are hard to carry, and you yourselves will not touch those loads with even one of your fingers.
en.R: Jesus answered, "How terrible for you experts in God's law too! You make people carry heavy loads of rules. But you yourselves will not even put one finger on those loads to help them.

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} dijo: «¡Ay también de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, los expertos en la ley! Porque {{plural_you:cargan|cargáis}} a {{gender:la gente|los hombres}} con cargas difíciles de llevar, y {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} mismos no {{plural_you:tocan|tocáis}} las cargas ni con uno de {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} dedos.
es.B: Él respondió: «¡Ay de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} también, expertos en la ley! {{plural_you:Ponen|Ponéis}} sobre {{gender:la gente|los hombres}} cargas difíciles de llevar, y {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} mismos no {{plural_you:tocan|tocáis}} esas cargas ni con un solo dedo.
es.R: Jesús respondió: «¡Qué terrible será también para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, expertos en la ley de Dios! {{plural_you:Obligan|Obligáis}} a la gente a llevar pesadas cargas de reglas. Pero {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} mismos no {{plural_you:ponen|ponéis}} ni un dedo sobre esas cargas para ayudar.

sw.L: Naye akasema, "Nanyi pia, wataalamu wa sheria, ole wenu! Kwa maana mnawabebesha watu mizigo iliyo migumu kubeba, lakini ninyi wenyewe hamuigusi mizigo hiyo hata kwa kidole chenu kimoja.
sw.B: Akasema, "Ole wenu ninyi pia wataalamu wa sheria! Mnawapakia watu mizigo iliyo migumu kubeba, nanyi wenyewe hamtaigusa mizigo hiyo hata kwa kidole kimoja.
sw.R: Yesu akajibu, "Itakuwa vibaya mno kwenu pia, wataalamu wa sheria ya Mungu! Mnawafanya watu wabebe mizigo mizito ya masharti. Lakini ninyi wenyewe hamtaweka hata kidole kimoja kwenye mizigo hiyo ili kuwasaidia.

decisions.choice: burdens hard to carry: demands about keeping the law that weigh people down
decisions.reason: The experts laid on people rules about how to keep the law. Peter later speaks of a yoke too heavy to bear (Acts 15:10).

decisions.choice: do not touch the burdens with a finger: do nothing to help carry them
alternatives: do not keep the rules themselves
decisions.reason: Most likely they give no help to those who struggle under the load. Some take it to mean that they find ways round the rules for themselves.

decisions.choice: Woe to you (L); How terrible for you (B, R)
decisions.reason: The same wording for every woe in 11:42-52 (see 11:42), as in 6:24-26.

decisions.choice: of rules; to help them
decisions.reason: Readable says what the loads are and why they should touch them.

decisions.choice: people as the default, men as the alternative
decisions.reason: The word means people in general.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus where the Greek has a pronoun or leaves the subject unstated, so young readers can follow who is acting.

source.text: οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, ὅτι οἰκοδομεῖτε τὰ μνημεῖα τῶν προφητῶν οἱ δὲ πατέρες ὑμῶν ἀπέκτειναν αὐτούς.

records.literal_gloss: Woe to you, for you build the tombs of the prophets, the and fathers of you killed them.

en.L: Woe to you, for you build the tombs of the prophets, and your fathers killed them.
en.B: How terrible for you! You build monuments over the prophets' graves, yet those prophets died at the hands of your ancestors.
en.R: How terrible for you! You build tombs to honor the prophets. But your own ancestors were the ones who killed those prophets.

es.L: ¡Ay de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}! Porque {{plural_you:edifican|edificáis}} los sepulcros de los profetas, y {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} padres los mataron.
es.B: ¡Ay de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}! {{plural_you:Levantan|Levantáis}} monumentos sobre los sepulcros de los profetas, y sin embargo fueron {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} antepasados quienes los mataron.
es.R: ¡Qué terrible será para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}! {{plural_you:Construyen|Construís}} tumbas para honrar a los profetas. Pero fueron {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} propios antepasados los que mataron a esos profetas.

sw.L: Ole wenu, kwa kuwa mnayajenga makaburi ya manabii, ilhali baba zenu waliwaua.
sw.B: Ole wenu! Mnajenga kumbukumbu juu ya makaburi ya manabii, ingawa manabii hao waliuawa na mababu zenu.
sw.R: Itakuwa vibaya mno kwenu! Mnajenga makaburi ili kuwaheshimu manabii. Lakini mababu zenu wenyewe ndio waliowaua manabii hao.

decisions.choice: build the tombs of the prophets: put up monuments to honor them
decisions.reason: The prophets had died long before. Building fine tombs over their graves was a way of honoring them.

decisions.choice: fathers: ancestors
decisions.reason: As in 6:23, 26. Israel had often rejected and killed its prophets (1 Kings 19:10; Jeremiah 26:20-23; Luke 13:34).

decisions.choice: Woe to you (L); How terrible for you (B, R)
decisions.reason: The same wording for every woe in 11:42-52 (see 11:42), as in 6:24-26.

decisions.choice: ancestors
decisions.reason: "Fathers" would suggest their parents.

decisions.choice: monuments over the prophets' graves (B); tombs to honor the prophets (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the building was for.

source.text: ἄρα μάρτυρές ἐστε καὶ συνευδοκεῖτε τοῖς ἔργοις τῶν πατέρων ὑμῶν, ὅτι αὐτοὶ μὲν ἀπέκτειναν αὐτοὺς ὑμεῖς δὲ οἰκοδομεῖτε.

records.literal_gloss: So witnesses you are and consent to the works of the fathers of you, for they indeed killed them, you now build.

en.L: So you are witnesses and approve of the works of your fathers, for they killed them, and you build [their tombs].
en.B: So you are witnesses, and you give your approval to what your ancestors did: they did the killing, and you do the building.
en.R: So you show that you agree with what your ancestors did. Your ancestors killed the prophets, and you build tombs for them.

es.L: Así que {{plural_you:son|sois}} testigos y {{plural_you:aprueban|aprobáis}} las obras de {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} padres, porque ellos los mataron, y {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:edifican|edificáis}} [sus sepulcros].
es.B: Así {{plural_you:son|sois}} testigos, y {{plural_you:dan|dais}} {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} aprobación a lo que hicieron {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} antepasados: ellos se encargaron de matar, y {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:se encargan|os encargáis}} de construir.
es.R: Así {{plural_you:muestran|mostráis}} que {{plural_you:están|estáis}} de acuerdo con lo que hicieron {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} antepasados. Ellos mataron a los profetas, y {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} les {{plural_you:construyen|construís}} tumbas.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo ninyi ni mashahidi, nanyi mnayaridhia matendo ya baba zenu, kwa sababu wao kweli waliwaua, nanyi mnajenga [makaburi yao].
sw.B: Kwa hiyo ninyi ni mashahidi, na mnayaunga mkono yale waliyotenda mababu zenu: wao waliua, nanyi mnajenga.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo mnaonyesha kwamba mnakubaliana na yale waliyotenda mababu zenu. Mababu zenu waliwaua manabii, nanyi mnawajengea makaburi.

decisions.choice: witnesses who approve: by building the tombs they finish what their ancestors began
alternatives: they honor the prophets and so condemn their ancestors
decisions.reason: Jesus turns their honoring of the prophets against them. Their ancestors killed the prophets; they bury them. They treat the living prophets of their own day as their ancestors did (11:49).

decisions.choice: you build: the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: you build their tombs, as in many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "their tombs" to complete the sentence. The shorter text is found in early manuscripts. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: they did the killing, and you do the building
alternatives: they killed them, and you build
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the sharp balance of the Greek.

decisions.choice: you show that you agree
decisions.reason: Readable says what being witnesses means here.

source.text: διὰ τοῦτο καὶ ἡ σοφία τοῦ θεοῦ εἶπεν· Ἀποστελῶ εἰς αὐτοὺς προφήτας καὶ ἀποστόλους, καὶ ἐξ αὐτῶν ἀποκτενοῦσιν καὶ διώξουσιν, ἵνα ἐκζητηθῇ τὸ αἷμα πάντων τῶν προφητῶν τὸ ἐκκεχυμένον ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου ἀπὸ τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης, ἀπὸ αἵματος Ἅβελ ἕως αἵματος Ζαχαρίου τοῦ ἀπολομένου μεταξὺ τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου καὶ τοῦ οἴκου· ναί, λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐκζητηθήσεται ἀπὸ τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης.

records.literal_gloss: Because of this also the Wisdom of God said, I will send to them prophets and apostles, and of them they will kill and persecute, \v 50 so that may be required the blood of all the prophets having been poured out from foundation of world from the generation this, \v 51 from blood of Abel to blood of Zechariah the [one] having perished between the altar and the house; yes, I say to you, it will be required from the generation this.

en.L: Because of this the Wisdom of God also said, 'I will send to them prophets and apostles, and [some] of them they will kill and persecute,' \v 50 so that the blood of all the prophets poured out since [the] foundation of [the] world may be required from this generation, \v 51 from [the] blood of Abel to [the] blood of Zechariah, who perished between the altar and the house. Yes, I tell you, it will be required from this generation.
en.B: That is why the Wisdom of God said, 'I will send them prophets and apostles. They will kill some of them and hunt down others.' \v 50 And so the blood of all the prophets shed since the world was founded will be charged to this generation, \v 51 from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zechariah, who died between the altar and the house of God. Yes, I tell you, this generation will be charged with it.
en.R: That is why the Wisdom of God said, 'I will send them prophets and apostles. They will kill some of them and treat others cruelly.' \v 50 So the people of this generation will be held guilty for the blood of all the prophets killed since the world began, \v 51 from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zechariah. Zechariah was killed between the altar and the house of God. Yes, I tell you, the people of this generation will be held guilty for it all.

es.L: Por esto también la Sabiduría de Dios dijo: “Enviaré a ellos profetas y apóstoles, y [a algunos] de ellos matarán y perseguirán”, \v 50 para que sea reclamada a esta generación la sangre de todos los profetas derramada desde [la] fundación del mundo, \v 51 desde [la] sangre de Abel hasta [la] sangre de Zacarías, que pereció entre el altar y la casa. Sí, {{plural_you:les|os}} digo, será reclamada a esta generación.
es.B: Por eso la Sabiduría de Dios dijo: “Les enviaré profetas y apóstoles. A algunos de ellos los matarán y a otros los perseguirán”. \v 50 Y así a esta generación se le pedirán cuentas por la sangre de todos los profetas derramada desde que el mundo fue fundado, \v 51 desde la sangre de Abel hasta la sangre de Zacarías, que murió entre el altar y la casa de Dios. Sí, {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que a esta generación se le pedirán cuentas por ella.
es.R: Por eso la Sabiduría de Dios dijo: “Les enviaré profetas y apóstoles. A algunos de ellos los matarán, y a otros los tratarán con crueldad”. \v 50 Así que la gente de esta generación será culpable de la sangre de todos los profetas asesinados desde que el mundo comenzó, \v 51 desde la sangre de Abel hasta la sangre de Zacarías. A Zacarías lo mataron entre el altar y la casa de Dios. Sí, {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que la gente de esta generación será tenida por culpable de todo eso.

sw.L: Kwa sababu hiyo Hekima ya Mungu pia ilisema, 'Nitawatuma kwao manabii na mitume, na [baadhi] yao watawaua na kuwafuatia kwa mateso,' \v 50 ili kizazi hiki kidaiwe damu ya manabii wote iliyomwagwa tangu ulimwengu ulipowekwa msingi, \v 51 kuanzia damu ya Habili mpaka damu ya Zakaria, aliyeangamia kati ya madhabahu na nyumba. Ndiyo, nawaambia, kizazi hiki kitadaiwa damu hiyo.
sw.B: Ndiyo maana Hekima ya Mungu ilisema, 'Nitawatumia manabii na mitume. Baadhi yao watawaua, na wengine watawawinda.' \v 50 Na hivyo kizazi hiki kitadaiwa damu ya manabii wote iliyomwagwa tangu ulimwengu ulipoumbwa, \v 51 kuanzia damu ya Habili hadi damu ya Zakaria, aliyeuawa kati ya madhabahu na nyumba ya Mungu. Ndiyo, nawaambia, kizazi hiki kitawajibika kwa damu hiyo.
sw.R: Ndiyo maana Hekima ya Mungu ilisema, 'Nitawatumia manabii na mitume. Baadhi yao watawaua, na wengine watawatendea ukatili.' \v 50 Kwa hiyo watu wa kizazi hiki watahesabiwa kuwa na hatia ya damu ya manabii wote waliouawa tangu ulimwengu ulipoanza, \v 51 kuanzia damu ya Habili hadi damu ya Zakaria. Zakaria aliuawa kati ya madhabahu na nyumba ya Mungu. Ndiyo, nawaambia, watu wa kizazi hiki watahesabiwa kuwa na hatia ya hayo yote.

decisions.choice: the Wisdom of God: God's wisdom, speaking as a person
alternatives: the title of a lost book
decisions.reason: Scripture pictures God's wisdom as a woman who calls out to people and is refused (Proverbs 1:20-33; 8:1-36). The words that follow are not found in any book of the Old Testament. They may sum up God's purpose as Scripture shows it (2 Chronicles 36:15-16), or come from a writing now lost. In Matthew 23:34 Jesus speaks them as his own: "I send".

decisions.choice: the quotation ends after "persecute"
alternatives: the quotation runs on to the end of the list in 11:51
decisions.reason: The Greek has no quotation marks. The words of Wisdom may end at 11:49, with Jesus drawing the conclusion in 11:50-51, or include 11:50-51a. "Yes, I tell you" is clearly Jesus speaking.

decisions.choice: apostles: messengers sent out
decisions.reason: The word means people sent with a message. Here it stands beside the prophets as God's messengers (compare 6:13).

decisions.choice: the blood required: called to account for murder
decisions.reason: To require someone's blood is to hold the killer to account (Genesis 9:5; 2 Samuel 4:11). As Zechariah died he prayed that the LORD would see it and call it to account (2 Chronicles 24:22). This generation, which rejects God's messengers as their ancestors did, will answer for it all.

decisions.choice: Abel to Zechariah: the first and the last murders told in the Scriptures
alternatives: Zechariah the prophet of the book of Zechariah
decisions.reason: Abel's blood cried out to God from the ground (Genesis 4:8-10). Zechariah son of Jehoiada was stoned in the court of the LORD's house for speaking God's word (2 Chronicles 24:20-22). In the traditional order of the Hebrew Scriptures, Chronicles comes last, so the two murders span the whole of Scripture.

decisions.choice: the house: the house of God, the temple building
decisions.reason: Zechariah died in the court of the house of the LORD (2 Chronicles 24:21), between the altar of burnt offering and the temple building itself.

decisions.choice: the world: the created world
decisions.reason: "Since the foundation of the world" means since the beginning of history.

decisions.choice: of God
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whose house it is.

decisions.choice: the words of Wisdom in single quotation marks inside Jesus' speech
decisions.reason: A quotation within speech takes single quotation marks.

decisions.choice: will be held guilty for
decisions.reason: Readable says what having blood required means.

decisions.choice: sea reclamada (L); se le pedirán cuentas (B)
decisions.reason: The blood is "required" of this generation: they are called to account for murder (meaning decision m4). Literal keeps the Greek passive; Balanced uses the Spanish idiom for being called to account, and Readable says they will be held guilty, as the English does.

decisions.choice: Hekima ya Mungu ilisema, with the agreement of the noun class
decisions.reason: Whether God's wisdom is spoken of here as a person is uncertain (meaning decision m1). The capital marks the personification, as the English does; the class agreement "ilisema" leaves the question open, where personal agreement ("alisema", as with "Neno" in John) would settle it.

source.text: οὐαὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς νομικοῖς, ὅτι ἤρατε τὴν κλεῖδα τῆς γνώσεως· αὐτοὶ οὐκ εἰσήλθατε καὶ τοὺς εἰσερχομένους ἐκωλύσατε.

records.literal_gloss: Woe to you the lawyers, for you took away the key of the knowledge; yourselves not did enter, and those entering you hindered.

en.L: Woe to you experts in the law, for you took away the key of knowledge; you yourselves did not enter, and you hindered those who were entering."
en.B: How terrible for you experts in the law! You have carried off the key of knowledge. You have not gone in yourselves, and you have stood in the way of those who were going in."
en.R: How terrible for you experts in God's law! You have taken away the key that opens the door to knowing God. You did not go in yourselves, and you stopped others who were trying to go in."

es.L: ¡Ay de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, los expertos en la ley! Porque {{plural_you:se llevaron|os llevasteis}} la llave del conocimiento; no {{plural_you:entraron|entrasteis}} {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} mismos, y {{plural_you:estorbaron|estorbasteis}} a los que iban entrando».
es.B: ¡Ay de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, expertos en la ley! {{plural_you:Se han llevado|Os habéis llevado}} la llave del conocimiento. {{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}} no {{plural_you:han|habéis}} entrado, y a los que iban entrando les {{plural_you:han|habéis}} cerrado el paso».
es.R: ¡Qué terrible será para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, expertos en la ley de Dios! {{plural_you:Se han llevado|Os habéis llevado}} la llave que abre la puerta para conocer a Dios. {{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}} no {{plural_you:entraron|entrasteis}}, y no {{plural_you:dejaron|dejasteis}} entrar a los que lo intentaban».

sw.L: Ole wenu wataalamu wa sheria, kwa maana mliuchukua ufunguo wa maarifa; ninyi wenyewe hamkuingia, na mkawazuia wale waliokuwa njiani kuingia."
sw.B: Ole wenu wataalamu wa sheria! Mmeubeba ufunguo wa maarifa mkaenda nao. Ninyi wenyewe hamkuingia, nanyi mmewazuia wale waliokuwa wakiingia."
sw.R: Itakuwa vibaya mno kwenu, wataalamu wa sheria ya Mungu! Mmechukua ufunguo unaofungua mlango wa kumjua Mungu. Ninyi wenyewe hamkuingia, na mliwazuia wengine waliokuwa wakijaribu kuingia."

decisions.choice: the key of knowledge: the key that opens the way to knowing God
decisions.reason: The experts held the key to the Scriptures, which lead to the knowledge of God and of his salvation (1:77). By their teaching they kept it from the people. What the door opens on is not stated.

decisions.choice: those entering: those who were trying to go in
alternatives: those who had already gone in
decisions.reason: The present tense describes people on the way in, whom the experts stopped.

decisions.choice: Woe to you (L); How terrible for you (B, R)
decisions.reason: The same wording for every woe in 11:42-52 (see 11:42), as in 6:24-26.

decisions.choice: the key that opens the door to knowing God
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the picture, following the first decision.

source.text: Κἀκεῖθεν ἐξελθόντος αὐτοῦ ἤρξαντο οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι δεινῶς ἐνέχειν καὶ ἀποστοματίζειν αὐτὸν περὶ πλειόνων, ἐνεδρεύοντες αὐτὸν θηρεῦσαί τι ἐκ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: From there having gone out him began the scribes and the Pharisees terribly to be hostile and to make him speak about many things, \v 54 lying in wait for him to catch something out of the mouth of him.

en.L: And when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went out from there, the scribes and the Pharisees began to be terribly hostile and to question {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} closely about many things, \v 54 lying in wait for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, to catch something from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mouth.
en.B: When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} left that place, the scribes and the Pharisees turned bitterly against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and kept pressing {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with questions about many things, \v 54 watching for a chance to trap {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own words.
en.R: When Jesus left there, the teachers of the law and the Pharisees became very hostile toward {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They began to ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} hard questions about many things. \v 54 They were trying to catch {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} saying something wrong.

es.L: Y saliendo {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} de allí, los escribas y los fariseos comenzaron a hostigar[lo] terriblemente y a hacerlo hablar de muchas cosas, \v 54 acechándolo para cazar algo de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} boca.
es.B: Cuando {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} salió de allí, los escribas y los fariseos se pusieron con saña en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} contra y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} acosaban con preguntas sobre muchas cosas, \v 54 vigilando para atraparlo en {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} propias palabras.
es.R: Cuando Jesús se fue de allí, los maestros de la ley y los fariseos se pusieron muy en contra de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Comenzaron a hacerle preguntas difíciles sobre muchas cosas. \v 54 Trataban de sorprenderlo diciendo algo malo.

sw.L: Na alipotoka huko, waandishi na Mafarisayo walianza kumshambulia vikali na kumbana kwa maswali juu ya mambo mengi, \v 54 wakimwekea mtego ili wakamate jambo fulani kutoka kinywani {{deity_pronoun:mwake|Mwake}}.
sw.B: Alipoondoka mahali hapo, waandishi na Mafarisayo walimgeukia kwa uchungu mkubwa, wakaendelea kumsonga kwa maswali juu ya mambo mengi, \v 54 wakingoja nafasi ya kumnasa kwa maneno {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} mwenyewe.
sw.R: Yesu alipoondoka huko, walimu wa sheria na Mafarisayo walimchukia sana. Wakaanza kumuuliza maswali magumu juu ya mambo mengi. \v 54 Walikuwa wakijaribu kumnasa aseme jambo baya.

decisions.choice: scribes: experts in the law of Moses
decisions.reason: As in 5:21. The scribes studied, taught and applied the law; Luke also calls them experts in the law (11:45).

decisions.choice: be terribly hostile: hold a fierce grudge, press hard against him
decisions.reason: The verb is used of Herodias's grudge against John (Mark 6:19).

decisions.choice: question closely: try to make him speak without thinking
decisions.reason: The verb means to draw someone out by questions, hoping for a careless answer.

decisions.choice: to catch something from his mouth: to trap him by something he says
decisions.reason: The words picture hunters lying in wait for prey.

decisions.choice: the shorter text, as in the SBLGNT
alternatives: a longer text in some manuscripts, adding that they sought a charge to bring against him
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add that they were seeking to catch him so that they might accuse him, and one ancient manuscript tells the scene in different words. The earliest manuscripts have the shorter text. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: teachers of the law (R); scribes (L, B)
decisions.reason: Today a scribe is someone who writes. Readable says what these men did.

decisions.choice: catch him saying something wrong
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus where the Greek has a pronoun or leaves the subject unstated, so young readers can follow who is acting.

decisions.choice: los escribas (L, B); los maestros de la ley (R)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet settles for the whole New Testament: "escribas" is the standard name for these experts in the law of Moses (meaning decision m1), and Readable says what they were.

decisions.choice: waandishi (L, B); walimu wa sheria (R)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet settles for the whole New Testament: "waandishi" is the standard name for these experts in the law of Moses (meaning decision m1), and Readable says what they were.
